## Financial Disclaimers, Human Verification & Cost Considerations

- Regulatory Disclaimer & Human Verification: Automated financial analysis outputs must include an explicit disclaimer stating that the report is for informational and research purposes only and does not constitute investment advice. Every extracted statement line item should store its exact page number and table coordinate so a human analyst can verify restatements, non-GAAP adjustments, and footnote contingencies.
- Cost Breakdown: SEC EDGAR API is 100% free. Parsing and analysing a 150-page 10-K report with Docling (https://github.com/docling-project/docling) and structured LLM extraction costs \~\$0.03–$0.08 per annual report on commercial APIs or \$0 using local Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama).

## Useful Tools, Documentation and GitHub Repositories

| Resource | Purpose | Type | Link |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SEC EDGAR API Docs | Free official XBRL JSON company financial facts | Official API | https://www.google.com/search?q=https://www.sec.gov/edgar/searchedgar/companysearch |
| Docling | High-precision PDF financial table extraction | Open-Source (MIT) | https://github.com/docling-project/docling |
| Aniket.app Valuation Case Study | Reference architecture for deterministic DCF engines | Case Study | https://aniket.app/ |

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why shouldn't I use standard chunk-based RAG alone to read financial statements?

Standard 500-token text chunking slices a Balance Sheet table in half, separating the table header (FY2025 | FY2024 ($ in millions)) from the bottom rows (Total Liabilities and Equity). Always extract entire financial tables intact using Docling (https://github.com/docling-project/docling) or fetch structured XBRL JSON directly from SEC EDGAR.

### How do I handle parenthetical negative numbers like `(45.2)` in PDF financial tables?

In accounting tables, parentheses denote negative values or cash outflows. Pre-process numeric table strings with a regex (r"^\(([0-9,\.]+)\)$") to convert (1,250.5) into -1250.5 before validation.

### What happens if a company's Balance Sheet doesn't balance after extraction?

Our Pydantic @model_validator (verify_accounting_identities) immediately raises a ValueError if $|\text{Assets} - (\text{Liabilities} + \text{Equity})| > 0.5\%$, triggering a re-extraction pass or flagging the filing for human review rather than computing corrupted ratios.

### How do I prevent the AI from mixing GAAP and Non-GAAP numbers?

Define distinct fields in your Pydantic schema (gaap_operating_income vs non_gaap_adjusted_ebitda) and instruct the extraction prompt to map strictly from the audited Consolidated Statements of Operations.

### Is the SEC EDGAR API free for commercial use?

Yes; SEC EDGAR filings and the /api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK{cik}.json API are public domain and free to query up to 10 requests per second, provided you pass a valid identifying User-Agent HTTP header.

### How do I handle Indian corporate annual reports (BSE/NSE PDF filings)?

For Indian companies reporting under Ind AS (typically in ₹ Crore or ₹ Lakh), set currency="INR" and unit_multiplier=10_000_000 (for Crore) or 100_000 (for Lakh) and parse the Consolidated Standalone/Group tables using Docling (https://github.com/docling-project/docling).

### Why does the DCF validator enforce `wacc > terminal_growth_rate`?

In the Gordon Growth terminal value formula $TV = \frac{FCF_n (1 + g)}{WACC - g}$, a terminal growth rate $g \ge WACC$ produces a negative or infinite enterprise value and is economically invalid.

### Can I export the AI Financial Analyst's output directly to an Excel model?

Yes; combine app/ratios.py and app/scenario_dcf.py with the openpyxl mutator from Article 2 to populate a live .xlsx valuation workbook automatically.

faqItems.question: Why is regex checking (`sql.startswith("SELECT")`) insufficient for SQL agent security?
faqItems.answer: Attackers or hallucinating LLMs can execute data-modifying statements inside a SELECT using PostgreSQL writable CTEs (WITH del AS (DELETE FROM users RETURNING *) SELECT * FROM del) or stacked queries (SELECT 1; DROP TABLE users). Only AST traversal via SQLGlot (https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot) combined with a read-only database user blocks these vectors reliably.

faqItems.question: How do I prevent an AI-generated SQL query from locking up my production database with a Cartesian join?
faqItems.answer: Always run the AI SQL agent against a read replica, enforce SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5000ms' inside the transaction, and run EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) prior to execution if the database contains multi-million-row tables.

faqItems.question: What happens if the LLM writes a column name that doesn't exist?
faqItems.answer: Wrap execute_safe_sqlite_query in a 2-attempt self-correction loop: catch OperationalError / ProgrammingError, pass the exact database error message (no such column: o.total_price) and the table DDL back to the LLM, and re-validate the repaired SQL through validate_and_rewrite_readonly_sql.

faqItems.question: How do I handle high-cardinality string filters (like `WHERE city = 'Bengaluru'` vs `'Bangalore'`)?
faqItems.answer: Index distinct categorical values of frequently filtered columns using trigram similarity (pg_trgm) or vector embeddings so the agent resolves the exact database string literal before generating the WHERE clause.

faqItems.question: Can SQLGlot translate queries if my LLM writes Postgres syntax for a SQLite or MySQL database?
faqItems.answer: Yes! Calling sqlglot.transpile(sql, read="postgres", write="sqlite")[0] automatically converts dialect-specific date arithmetic, type casts, and identifier quotes.

faqItems.question: Is Vanna AI still maintained in 2026?
faqItems.answer: Per its official GitHub repository (vanna-ai/vanna (https://github.com/vanna-ai/vanna)), the repository was archived by its owner on March 29, 2026 and is now read-only. New projects should build directly on actively maintained primitives like SQLGlot (https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot), LangGraph (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph), and SQLAlchemy (https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy).

faqItems.question: How do I enforce multi-tenant data isolation in a SaaS AI SQL Agent?
faqItems.answer: Use PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON orders USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id')::uuid)) and set SET LOCAL app.current_tenant_id = '...' from your authenticated FastAPI session before executing the query.

body:
## Introduction

To build an AI SQL agent that translates natural-language questions into accurate PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite queries without exposing your database to destructive mutations or runaway full-table scans, you must implement three mandatory defence-in-depth layers: (1) AST-level SQL parsing and linting using [SQLGlot](https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot) to block any non-SELECT statement or unauthorized table access before execution, (2) database-enforced read-only transactions with statement timeouts, and (3) schema pruning with bounded self-correction loops.

> [!TIP]
> **Architecture Reference:** Internal Link Suggestion: On Aniket.app (https://aniket.app/), see the [[Prompt BI](/projects/prompt-bi/)](/projects/prompt-bi/) engineering system overview for how AST query linting blocks unsafe SQL mutations in production analytics pipelines, and cross-reference [Article 10: How to Build an AI Data Analyst ](/writing/build-ai-data-analyst-csv-charts-pandas/).

## Natural-Language-to-SQL Architecture & Security Boundaries

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Question([User Natural Language Question]) --> Ambiguity{Ambiguity & Schema Matcher}
    Ambiguity -- "Missing Metric Definition" --> Clarify([Ask User for Clarification])
    Ambiguity -- "Clear Intent" --> SchemaPruner[DDL & Few-Shot SQL Retriever]
    SchemaPruner --> Generator[LLM SQL Generator]
    Generator --> ASTValidator{SQLGlot AST Linter: Single SELECT + Allowed Tables + LIMIT}
    ASTValidator -- "Blocked DDL/DML or Syntax Error" --> Generator
    ASTValidator -- "Valid Read-Only AST" --> Executor[(Read-Only DB Session + Timeout)]
    Executor -- "Database Execution Error & retries < 2" --> Generator
    Executor -- "Query Result Rows" --> Explainer[Natural Language Summary & Chart Spec]
```

### Why Regex Filtering Fails and SQLGlot AST Validation Is Required

Many naive tutorials check if sql.upper().startswith("SELECT"): before executing LLM-generated SQL. That check is trivially bypassed by stacked queries (SELECT 1; DROP TABLE users;), writable Common Table Expressions (WITH deleted AS (DELETE FROM orders RETURNING *) SELECT * FROM deleted;), or system catalog functions (pg_read_file()). Parsing the query into an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) with SQLGlot (https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot) lets you inspect every node in the tree deterministically, verify that the root expression is strictly exp.Select, confirm zero Delete/Update/Drop/Insert/Command nodes exist anywhere in the tree, verify every exp.Table against an allowlist, and automatically inject a LIMIT 100 cap.

## Technology Comparison: Paid vs. Open-Source Stack

> Repository Verification Note: While vanna-ai/vanna (https://github.com/vanna-ai/vanna) (MIT License, 23.8k stars) is a well-known open-source Text-to-SQL framework, our repository audit on October 30, 2026 confirmed that `vanna-ai/vanna` was archived by its owner on March 29, 2026 and is now read-only. For actively maintained production systems in 2026, we recommend building a clean pipeline with **SQLGlot** (https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot) + **SQLAlchemy** (https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy) + **LangGraph** (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph) / Pydantic.

| Component | Commercial / Managed Service | Open-Source Alternative | Self-Hosting Possible? | Maintenance & Technical Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SQL AST Parser & Linter | Proprietary BI Gateways | SQLGlot (https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot) (MIT License, active, 9.7k stars) | Yes | Zero dependencies; parses and transpiles 30+ SQL dialects including Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, DuckDB, and Snowflake. |
| Text-to-SQL Orchestration | Snowflake Cortex Analyst / Databricks Genie | LangGraph (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph) (MIT, active) / Vanna (https://github.com/vanna-ai/vanna) (MIT, *archived Mar 29, 2026*) | Yes | Custom LangGraph + SQLGlot gives full control over AST security and dialect transpilation. |
| Database Engine | AWS RDS / Supabase / Neon | PostgreSQL (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/) / MySQL / SQLite + SQLAlchemy (https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy) (MIT) | Yes | Always connect using a dedicated readonly_ai_user database role. |
| SQL Generation LLM | OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini / gpt-4.1) / Claude | Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B / SeekCoder) | Yes | Coding-tuned open-weight models (Qwen2.5-Coder) match commercial models on multi-join SQL generation. |

### Recommended Implementation Options

### Option A: Best Practical Implementation (Recommended): Python 3.12 + FastAPI + SQLGlot (https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot) AST validator + SQLAlchemy (https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy) read-only connection pool + OpenAI Structured Outputs (or Qwen2.5-Coder-32B).

### Option B: Fully Open-Source Local Implementation: SQLGlot (https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot) + SQLAlchemy (https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy) + PostgreSQL/SQLite + local Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (qwen2.5-coder:14b or 32b).

### Option C: Production Enterprise Analytics Stack: FastAPI + PostgreSQL read replica + SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5000ms' + pgvector few-shot query bank + tenant row-level security (RLS).

## Step-by-Step Implementation Guide

### Step 1: Project Structure

```text
ai-sql-agent/
├── app/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── ast_guard.py
│   ├── db_executor.py
│   └── sql_agent.py
├── tests/
│   └── test_sql_agent.py

```

### Step 2: Install Dependencies

```bash
pip install sqlglot==25.24.0 sqlalchemy==2.0.35 pydantic==2.9.2 openai==1.51.0 pytest==8.3.3
```

### Step 3: Implement the SQLGlot AST Security Linter (app/ast_guard.py)

This module parses raw SQL into an AST, rejects multi-statement injections, bans DDL/DML mutations anywhere in the tree, verifies referenced tables against an allowlist, blocks dangerous system functions, and enforces a row limit:

```python
from typing import Set
import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp

FORBIDDEN_AST_NODES = (
    exp.Insert,
    exp.Update,
    exp.Delete,
    exp.Drop,
    exp.Create,
    exp.Alter,
    exp.Command,
    exp.Grant,
    exp.Revoke,
    exp.Transaction,
    exp.Commit,
    exp.Rollback,
    exp.Copy,
    exp.Pragma,
)

FORBIDDEN_FUNCTIONS = {
    "pg_read_file",
    "pg_ls_dir",
    "pg_execute_server_program",
    "pg_sleep",
    "dblink",
    "lo_import",
    "lo_export",
    "load_extension",
}

def validate_and_rewrite_readonly_sql(
    raw_sql: str,
    allowed_tables: Set[str],
    dialect: str = "postgres",
    max_limit: int = 100,
) -> str:
    """Validates SQL via SQLGlot AST inspection and enforces a hard LIMIT cap."""
    try:
        parsed_statements = sqlglot.parse(raw_sql, read=dialect)
    except sqlglot.errors.ParseError as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"SQL syntax parse error: {exc}") from exc

    # 1. Block stacked multi-statement queries (e.g. SELECT 1; DROP TABLE x;)
    non_empty_stmts = [s for s in parsed_statements if s is not None]
    if len(non_empty_stmts) != 1:
        raise PermissionError("Exactly one SQL statement is permitted per query.")

    ast = non_empty_stmts[0]

    # 2. Root expression must be a SELECT or UNION of SELECTs
    if not isinstance(ast, (exp.Select, exp.Union)):
        raise PermissionError(f"Only SELECT queries are permitted. Found root: {type(ast).__name__}")

    # 3. Walk the entire AST to block writable CTEs or DDL/DML nodes
    for node in ast.walk():
        if isinstance(node, FORBIDDEN_AST_NODES):
            raise PermissionError(f"Forbidden SQL operation detected in AST: {type(node).__name__}")
        if isinstance(node, exp.Anonymous) and node.name.lower() in FORBIDDEN_FUNCTIONS:
            raise PermissionError(f"Forbidden database function called: {node.name}")
        if isinstance(node, exp.Func) and node.sql_name().lower() in FORBIDDEN_FUNCTIONS:
            raise PermissionError(f"Forbidden database function called: {node.sql_name()}")

    # 4. Allowlist check on every referenced table (excluding CTE aliases)
    cte_aliases = {cte.alias_or_name.lower() for cte in ast.find_all(exp.CTE)}
    allowed_lower = {t.lower() for t in allowed_tables}

    for table_node in ast.find_all(exp.Table):
        tbl_name = table_node.name.lower()
        if tbl_name not in cte_aliases and tbl_name not in allowed_lower:
            raise PermissionError(f"Query references unauthorized or unknown table: '{table_node.name}'")

    # 5. Enforce or cap LIMIT clause on top-level SELECT
    if isinstance(ast, exp.Select):
        existing_limit = ast.args.get("limit")
        if existing_limit is None:
            ast = ast.limit(max_limit)
        else:
            try:
                limit_val = int(existing_limit.expression.name)
                if limit_val > max_limit:
                    ast = ast.limit(max_limit)
            except (ValueError, AttributeError):
                ast = ast.limit(max_limit)

    return ast.sql(dialect=dialect)
```

### Step 4: Implement Read-Only Database Execution (app/db_executor.py)

For SQLite, we open the database using mode=ro URI or PRAGMA query_only = ON. For PostgreSQL, we execute SET LOCAL TRANSACTION READ ONLY; and SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5000ms';:

```python
import sqlite3
from typing import List, Dict, Any, Set
from app.ast_guard import validate_and_rewrite_readonly_sql

def execute_safe_sqlite_query(
    db_path: str,
    raw_sql: str,
    allowed_tables: Set[str],
    max_limit: int = 100,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Validates SQL via SQLGlot AST and executes it against a read-only SQLite connection."""
    safe_sql = validate_and_rewrite_readonly_sql(
        raw_sql=raw_sql,
        allowed_tables=allowed_tables,
        dialect="sqlite",
        max_limit=max_limit,
    )
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=5.0)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        conn.execute("PRAGMA query_only = ON;")
        cursor = conn.execute(safe_sql)
        rows = [dict(row) for row in cursor.fetchall()]
        columns = [desc[0] for desc in cursor.description] if cursor.description else []
        return {
            "executed_sql": safe_sql,
            "columns": columns,
            "row_count": len(rows),
            "rows": rows,
        }
    finally:
        conn.close()
```

## Testing the AI SQL Agent (tests/test_sql_agent.py)

```python
import sqlite3
import pytest
from app.ast_guard import validate_and_rewrite_readonly_sql
from app.db_executor import execute_safe_sqlite_query

ALLOWED = {"customers", "orders", "order_items"}

def test_ast_guard_blocks_stacked_queries_and_writable_ctes():
    # Block stacked DROP TABLE
    with pytest.raises(PermissionError, match="Exactly one SQL statement"):
        validate_and_rewrite_readonly_sql("SELECT * FROM orders; DROP TABLE orders;", ALLOWED)

    # Block writable CTE
    with pytest.raises(PermissionError, match="Forbidden SQL operation"):
        validate_and_rewrite_readonly_sql(
            "WITH d AS (DELETE FROM orders RETURNING *) SELECT * FROM d", ALLOWED
        )

    # Block unauthorized table (e.g., payroll_salaries)
    with pytest.raises(PermissionError, match="unauthorized or unknown table"):
        validate_and_rewrite_readonly_sql("SELECT * FROM payroll_salaries", ALLOWED)

def test_ast_guard_allows_cte_and_injects_limit():
    sql = """
    WITH regional_totals AS (
        SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_spent
        FROM orders
        GROUP BY customer_id
    )
    SELECT c.name, r.total_spent
    FROM customers c
    JOIN regional_totals r ON c.id = r.customer_id
    ORDER BY r.total_spent DESC
    """
    safe_sql = validate_and_rewrite_readonly_sql(sql, ALLOWED, dialect="sqlite", max_limit=50)
    assert "LIMIT 50" in safe_sql

def test_end_to_end_readonly_sqlite_execution(tmp_path):
    db_file = str(tmp_path / "analytics.db")
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_file)
    conn.executescript(
        """
        CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, region TEXT);
        CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, amount REAL);
        INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Acme Corp', 'APAC'), (2, 'Globex', 'NA');
        INSERT INTO orders VALUES (101, 1, 450.0), (102, 1, 550.0), (103, 2, 300.0);
        """
    )
    conn.close()

    res = execute_safe_sqlite_query(
        db_file,
        "SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.name",
        allowed_tables={"customers", "orders"},
    )
    assert res["row_count"] == 2
    assert res["rows"][0]["revenue"] == 1000.0
```

## Handling Ambiguous Questions, Query Optimisation & Cost

- Handling Ambiguous Questions: When a user asks *"Who are our top customers?"*, the term "top" could mean highest gross revenue, highest net margin, or highest order count. Include an ambiguity classification field (is_ambiguous: bool, clarification_question: Optional[str]) in the agent's structured output schema so it asks *"Would you like top customers ranked by gross order revenue or total order count?"* when metric definitions are unspecified.
- Schema Pruning for Large Databases: If an enterprise database has 400 tables, passing all 400 CREATE TABLE DDLs overflows the prompt and degrades join accuracy. Embed table descriptions into pgvector (https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector) and retrieve only the top 8–10 relevant table schemas plus foreign-key neighbours per query.

## Useful Tools, Documentation and GitHub Repositories

| Resource | Purpose | Type | Link |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SQLGlot | Python SQL AST parser, linter, optimizer, and transpiler | Open-Source (MIT) | https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot |
| SQLAlchemy | Python SQL toolkit and database connection pooling | Open-Source (MIT) | https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy |
| PostgreSQL Docs | Read-only roles, row-level security, and statement timeouts | Documentation | https://www.postgresql.org/docs/ |
| Vanna (Archived) | Historical Text-to-SQL reference (*archived Mar 29, 2026*) | Open-Source (MIT) | https://github.com/vanna-ai/vanna |

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why is regex checking (`sql.startswith("SELECT")`) insufficient for SQL agent security?

Attackers or hallucinating LLMs can execute data-modifying statements inside a SELECT using PostgreSQL writable CTEs (WITH del AS (DELETE FROM users RETURNING *) SELECT * FROM del) or stacked queries (SELECT 1; DROP TABLE users). Only AST traversal via SQLGlot (https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot) combined with a read-only database user blocks these vectors reliably.

### How do I prevent an AI-generated SQL query from locking up my production database with a Cartesian join?

Always run the AI SQL agent against a read replica, enforce SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5000ms' inside the transaction, and run EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) prior to execution if the database contains multi-million-row tables.

### What happens if the LLM writes a column name that doesn't exist?

Wrap execute_safe_sqlite_query in a 2-attempt self-correction loop: catch OperationalError / ProgrammingError, pass the exact database error message (no such column: o.total_price) and the table DDL back to the LLM, and re-validate the repaired SQL through validate_and_rewrite_readonly_sql.

### How do I handle high-cardinality string filters (like `WHERE city = 'Bengaluru'` vs `'Bangalore'`)?

Index distinct categorical values of frequently filtered columns using trigram similarity (pg_trgm) or vector embeddings so the agent resolves the exact database string literal before generating the WHERE clause.

### Can SQLGlot translate queries if my LLM writes Postgres syntax for a SQLite or MySQL database?

Yes! Calling sqlglot.transpile(sql, read="postgres", write="sqlite")[0] automatically converts dialect-specific date arithmetic, type casts, and identifier quotes.

### Is Vanna AI still maintained in 2026?

Per its official GitHub repository (vanna-ai/vanna (https://github.com/vanna-ai/vanna)), the repository was archived by its owner on March 29, 2026 and is now read-only. New projects should build directly on actively maintained primitives like SQLGlot (https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot), LangGraph (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph), and SQLAlchemy (https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy).

### How do I enforce multi-tenant data isolation in a SaaS AI SQL Agent?

Use PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON orders USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id')::uuid)) and set SET LOCAL app.current_tenant_id = '...' from your authenticated FastAPI session before executing the query.

### Which open-weight local model is best for Text-to-SQL?

Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct (or the 14B variant on 16GB GPUs) via Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) delivers outstanding multi-table join accuracy and adheres strictly to schema constraints.

faqItems.question: Why does the agent profile the CSV first instead of passing the CSV file directly to the LLM?
faqItems.answer: A 50,000-row CSV contains millions of tokens—exceeding context limits and costing dollars per query—while LLMs frequently miscalculate averages over raw text. Passing a 600-token statistical schema profile (dtypes, min, max, null_count, top_values) costs 99.9% less and allows Pandas to compute exact floating-point aggregations.

faqItems.question: Is Python's `ast` check alone enough to sandbox untrusted multi-tenant users?
faqItems.answer: ast inspection is your first line of defence against accidental file writes, network calls, and dunder attribute escapes. In a public multi-tenant SaaS app, always run the validated Python snippet inside an unprivileged container (Docker with --network none --read-only --memory 512m) or microVM.

faqItems.question: How do I handle CSV files that fail with `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte`?
faqItems.answer: Attempt reading with encoding="utf-8-sig" first (to handle Excel BOM markers), and fall back to charset_normalizer or encoding="latin1".

faqItems.question: How do I prevent Matplotlib memory leaks in a long-running FastAPI server?
faqItems.answer: Always set matplotlib.use("Agg") at startup and call plt.close(fig) inside a finally block after saving every chart.

faqItems.question: What if the CSV is 5GB and doesn't fit in Pandas memory?
faqItems.answer: Swap pd.read_csv() for DuckDB (duckdb.sql("SELECT Segment, SUM(ARR) FROM 'large_file.csv' GROUP BY Segment").df()), which streams out-of-core aggregations over multi-gigabyte CSVs using minimal RAM.

faqItems.question: How do I stop the LLM from picking the wrong chart type (like a pie chart with 40 slices)?
faqItems.answer: Encode chart-selection rules in the system prompt: use bar charts for categorical comparisons (<= 12 categories), line charts for continuous time series, and histograms/boxplots for distributions; ban pie charts whenever category count exceeds 5.

faqItems.question: Can I return interactive charts for a web dashboard instead of static PNGs?
faqItems.answer: Yes; instruct the agent to output a Vega-Lite or Plotly JSON specification populated with the aggregated result dictionary, which your React frontend renders interactively without executing arbitrary JavaScript.

faqItems.question: How do I handle missing values (`NaN`) before running statistical correlations?
faqItems.answer: Report the exact null_count per column in the profile and explicitly log whether rows with NaN were dropped (dropna()) or imputed (fillna(median)) in the cleaning_actions audit trail.

body:
## Introduction

To build an AI data analyst that ingests arbitrary CSV files, cleans dirty columns, runs statistical hypothesis tests, and generates publication-grade charts in response to natural-language questions, you must never pass raw CSV rows into the LLM prompt or call unrestricted exec() on AI-generated Python code. Real-world CSVs contain hundreds of thousands of rows, mixed encodings (UTF-8-SIG, Latin-1), currency strings ("$1,420.50"), and missing values. Instead, your architecture should extract a compact statistical schema profile, let the LLM generate AST-validated Pandas/Matplotlib analysis scripts (or declarative analysis specifications), execute them in an isolated subprocess with strict resource and import allowlists, and return both the verifiable numerical table and the rendered chart image.

> [!TIP]
> **Architecture Reference:** Internal Link Suggestion: Compare this CSV/DataFrame pipeline with [Article 2: How to Build an AI Excel Agent and [Article 9: How to Build an AI SQL Agent ](/writing/build-ai-excel-agent-spreadsheets-analysis/](/writing/build-ai-sql-agent-natural-language-database-queries/)).

## System Architecture: Profiling, AST-Validated Execution & Chart Generation

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CSV([User Uploads CSV + Natural Language Question]) --> Ingest[Encoding & Delimiter Detector + Pandas Loader]
    Ingest --> Cleaner[Automated Data Cleaner: Dates, Currencies, Duplicates]
    Cleaner --> Profiler[Statistical Schema Profiler: Dtypes, Quantiles, Nulls]
    Profiler --> CodeGen[LLM Analysis & Chart Code Generator]
    CodeGen --> ASTCheck{Python AST Security Validator: Allowed Imports Only}
    ASTCheck -- "Forbidden Import / OS Call" --> CodeGen
    ASTCheck -- "Safe Pandas/Matplotlib AST" --> Sandbox[Isolated Subprocess Runner with Timeout]
    Sandbox --> Artifacts([Verified JSON Metrics + High-DPI PNG Chart])
```

### Securing AI-Generated Python Code

When an LLM writes Python code to group a DataFrame and plot a chart, executing that code blindly on your server allows remote code execution (import os; os.system(...) or open('/etc/passwd')). Before executing any AI-generated analysis snippet:

1. Parse the code using Python's built-in ast.parse().
1. Walk every AST node and allow imports strictly from { "pandas", "numpy", "matplotlib", "matplotlib.pyplot", "seaborn", "scipy.stats" }.
1. Block all calls to eval, exec, open, compile, __import__, getattr, setattr, os, sys, subprocess, socket, and pathlib.
1. Run the validated calculation inside a child process with a hard timeout (timeout=15s) and a read-only reference to the cleaned DataFrame.

## Technology Comparison: Paid vs. Open-Source Stack

| Component | Commercial / Managed Solution | Open-Source Alternative | Self-Hosting Possible? | Technical Limitations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DataFrame & OLAP Engine | Snowflake / BigQuery | Pandas (https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas) (BSD-3-Clause) / DuckDB (MIT) | Yes | For CSVs >500MB, use DuckDB or Polars to avoid out-of-memory errors. |
| Charting & Visualisation | Tableau / PowerBI Embedded | Matplotlib (PSF) / Seaborn (BSD-3) / Plotly (MIT) | Yes | Always set plt.tight_layout() and dpi=200 to prevent clipped axis labels. |
| Code Sandbox | E2B Cloud Code Interpreter | Python ast Allowlist + Linux bubblewrap / Docker Sandbox | Yes | ast validation must be paired with OS-level process isolation in multi-tenant production. |
| Interactive Dashboard | Retool / Hex | Streamlit (Apache-2.0) / FastAPI + React | Yes | Streamlit reruns the script on interaction unless @st.cache_data is applied. |

### Recommended Implementation Options

### Option A: Best Practical Implementation (Recommended): Python 3.12 + Pandas (https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas) + Matplotlib/Seaborn + Python ast security validator + OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini or gpt-4.1) + FastAPI/Streamlit.

### Option B: Fully Open-Source Local Implementation: Pandas (https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas) + Matplotlib + local Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (qwen2.5-coder:32b).

### Option C: Production Multi-Tenant Implementation: FastAPI + DuckDB for zero-copy Parquet/CSV analytics + ephemeral gVisor/Docker worker containers for code execution.

## Step-by-Step Implementation Guide

### Step 1: Project Structure

```text
ai-data-analyst/
├── app/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── cleaner_profiler.py
│   ├── sandbox_runner.py
│   └── chart_generator.py
├── tests/
│   └── test_data_analyst.py
└── requirements.txt
```

### Step 2: Implement Automated CSV Cleaning and Profiling (app/cleaner_profiler.py)

```python
from typing import Dict, Any
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def clean_and_profile_dataframe(df: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Cleans whitespace, coerces currency/numeric strings, and extracts a compact statistical profile."""
    cleaned = df.copy()
    cleaning_actions = []

    # 1. Strip column name whitespace
    cleaned.columns = [str(c).strip() for c in cleaned.columns]

    # 2. Drop exact duplicate rows
    dup_count = int(cleaned.duplicated().sum())
    if dup_count > 0:
        cleaned = cleaned.drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)
        cleaning_actions.append(f"Dropped {dup_count} duplicate rows.")

    # 3. Coerce currency/percentage object columns where >80% parse as numeric
    for col in cleaned.select_dtypes(include=["object"]).columns:
        sample_non_null = cleaned[col].dropna().astype(str).str.strip()
        if len(sample_non_null) == 0:
            continue
        stripped = sample_non_null.str.replace(r"^[\$₹€£,]+|%$", "", regex=True).str.replace(",", "", regex=False)
        coerced = pd.to_numeric(stripped, errors="coerce")
        if coerced.notna().mean() >= 0.85:
            cleaned[col] = pd.to_numeric(
                cleaned[col].astype(str).str.replace(r"[\$₹€£,%]", "", regex=True).str.strip(),
                errors="coerce",
            )
            cleaning_actions.append(f"Converted column '{col}' from string to float.")

    # 4. Build compact profile for the LLM
    col_profiles = {}
    for col in cleaned.columns:
        series = cleaned[col]
        info: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "dtype": str(series.dtype),
            "null_count": int(series.isna().sum()),
            "unique_count": int(series.nunique(dropna=True)),
        }
        if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(series):
            desc = series.describe()
            info["mean"] = round(float(desc.get("mean", 0.0)), 4) if not np.isnan(desc.get("mean", np.nan)) else None
            info["std"] = round(float(desc.get("std", 0.0)), 4) if not np.isnan(desc.get("std", np.nan)) else None
            info["min"] = float(desc.get("min", 0.0)) if not np.isnan(desc.get("min", np.nan)) else None
            info["max"] = float(desc.get("max", 0.0)) if not np.isnan(desc.get("max", np.nan)) else None
        else:
            info["top_values"] = series.dropna().astype(str).value_counts().head(5).to_dict()
        col_profiles[col] = info

    profile = {
        "row_count": int(len(cleaned)),
        "column_count": int(len(cleaned.columns)),
        "cleaning_actions": cleaning_actions,
        "columns": col_profiles,
    }
    return cleaned, profile
```

### Step 3: Implement the AST-Validated Python Analysis & Chart Runner (app/sandbox_runner.py)

```python
import ast
from typing import Dict, Any, Set
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

ALLOWED_MODULES: Set[str] = {"pandas", "numpy", "matplotlib", "matplotlib.pyplot", "math"}
FORBIDDEN_CALL_NAMES: Set[str] = {
    "eval", "exec", "open", "compile", "__import__", "getattr", "setattr",
    "delattr", "globals", "locals", "input", "breakpoint", "system", "popen",
}
FORBIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES: Set[str] = {
    "to_pickle", "read_pickle", "to_sql", "to_csv", "to_excel", "system",
    "__subclasses__", "__bases__", "__globals__", "__code__",
}

def validate_analysis_code_ast(code_str: str) -> None:
    """Inspects the Python AST to block file I/O, network access, and disallowed imports."""
    tree = ast.parse(code_str)
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            for alias in node.names:
                if alias.name not in ALLOWED_MODULES:
                    raise PermissionError(f"Disallowed import: {alias.name}")
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
            if not node.module or node.module not in ALLOWED_MODULES:
                raise PermissionError(f"Disallowed import from: {node.module}")
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
            if isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) and node.func.id in FORBIDDEN_CALL_NAMES:
                raise PermissionError(f"Disallowed function call: {node.func.id}")
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
            if node.attr in FORBIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES or node.attr.startswith("__"):
                raise PermissionError(f"Disallowed attribute access: {node.attr}")

def execute_verified_analysis(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    code_str: str,
    chart_output_path: str | None = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Validates `code_str`, runs it against a copy of `df`, and saves `fig` if generated."""
    validate_analysis_code_ast(code_str)
    plt.close("all")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5), dpi=150)

    safe_locals: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "df": df.copy(deep=True),
        "pd": pd,
        "np": np,
        "plt": plt,
        "fig": fig,
        "ax": ax,
        "result": None,
    }
    safe_builtins = {
        "len": len, "round": round, "min": min, "max": max, "sum": sum,
        "abs": abs, "float": float, "int": int, "str": str, "dict": dict, "list": list,
    }
    exec(code_str, {"__builtins__": safe_builtins}, safe_locals)

    saved_chart = None
    if chart_output_path and len(ax.patches) + len(ax.lines) + len(ax.collections) > 0:
        fig.tight_layout()
        fig.savefig(chart_output_path, dpi=150)
        saved_chart = chart_output_path
    plt.close(fig)

    res = safe_locals.get("result")
    if isinstance(res, pd.DataFrame):
        res = res.to_dict(orient="records")
    elif isinstance(res, pd.Series):
        res = res.to_dict()

    return {"result": res, "chart_path": saved_chart}
```

## Testing the AI Data Analyst (tests/test_data_analyst.py)

```python
import os
import pandas as pd
import pytest
from app.cleaner_profiler import clean_and_profile_dataframe
from app.sandbox_runner import validate_analysis_code_ast, execute_verified_analysis

def test_csv_cleaner_and_profiler():
    raw_df = pd.DataFrame({
        " Category ": ["Cloud", "Cloud", "Edge", "AI"],
        "Revenue_USD": ["$1,200.50", "$1,200.50", "$850.00", "$2,400.00"],
    })
    cleaned, profile = clean_and_profile_dataframe(raw_df)
    assert profile["row_count"] == 3  # Duplicate row dropped
    assert cleaned["Revenue_USD"].dtype == float
    assert profile["columns"]["Revenue_USD"]["max"] == 2400.0

def test_ast_sandbox_blocks_os_and_dunder_escapes():
    with pytest.raises(PermissionError, match="Disallowed import"):
        validate_analysis_code_ast("import os\nos.system('ls')")
    with pytest.raises(PermissionError, match="Disallowed function call"):
        validate_analysis_code_ast("open('/etc/passwd').read()")
    with pytest.raises(PermissionError, match="Disallowed attribute access"):
        validate_analysis_code_ast("x = df.__class__.__bases__")

def test_verified_pandas_aggregation_and_chart_export(tmp_path):
    df = pd.DataFrame({
        "Segment": ["Enterprise", "SMB", "Enterprise", "SMB"],
        "ARR": [150000, 40000, 210000, 60000],
    })
    code = """
grouped = df.groupby('Segment')['ARR'].sum()
grouped.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax, title='Total ARR by Segment')
result = grouped
"""
    chart_file = str(tmp_path / "arr_chart.png")
    out = execute_verified_analysis(df, code, chart_output_path=chart_file)
    assert out["result"] == {"Enterprise": 360000, "SMB": 100000}
    assert os.path.exists(chart_file)
```

## Troubleshooting, Reproducibility & Cost Considerations

- Ensuring Data Reproducibility: Along with every chart and summary answer, return the exact Pandas code snippet and the SHA-256 hash of the input CSV so any data scientist can reproduce the exact numbers independently.
- Cost Breakdown: Because the LLM only reads the JSON statistical profile (\~600 tokens) and outputs a 10-line Pandas snippet (\~150 tokens), analysing 1,000 CSV questions/month costs <\$0.50/month on commercial APIs or \$0 on local Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama).

## Useful Tools, Documentation and GitHub Repositories

| Resource | Purpose | Type | Link |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pandas | Tabular data cleaning, aggregation, and time-series analysis | Open-Source (BSD-3) | https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas |
| Matplotlib | High-DPI programmatic chart rendering | Open-Source (PSF) | https://www.google.com/search?q=https://matplotlib.org/stable/index.html |
| Ollama | Local execution of Qwen2.5-Coder for Pandas code generation | Open-Source (MIT) | https://github.com/ollama/ollama |

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why does the agent profile the CSV first instead of passing the CSV file directly to the LLM?

A 50,000-row CSV contains millions of tokens—exceeding context limits and costing dollars per query—while LLMs frequently miscalculate averages over raw text. Passing a 600-token statistical schema profile (dtypes, min, max, null_count, top_values) costs 99.9% less and allows Pandas to compute exact floating-point aggregations.

### Is Python's `ast` check alone enough to sandbox untrusted multi-tenant users?

ast inspection is your first line of defence against accidental file writes, network calls, and dunder attribute escapes. In a public multi-tenant SaaS app, always run the validated Python snippet inside an unprivileged container (Docker with --network none --read-only --memory 512m) or microVM.

### How do I handle CSV files that fail with `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte`?

Attempt reading with encoding="utf-8-sig" first (to handle Excel BOM markers), and fall back to charset_normalizer or encoding="latin1".

### How do I prevent Matplotlib memory leaks in a long-running FastAPI server?

Always set matplotlib.use("Agg") at startup and call plt.close(fig) inside a finally block after saving every chart.

### What if the CSV is 5GB and doesn't fit in Pandas memory?

Swap pd.read_csv() for DuckDB (duckdb.sql("SELECT Segment, SUM(ARR) FROM 'large_file.csv' GROUP BY Segment").df()), which streams out-of-core aggregations over multi-gigabyte CSVs using minimal RAM.

### How do I stop the LLM from picking the wrong chart type (like a pie chart with 40 slices)?

Encode chart-selection rules in the system prompt: use bar charts for categorical comparisons (<= 12 categories), line charts for continuous time series, and histograms/boxplots for distributions; ban pie charts whenever category count exceeds 5.

### Can I return interactive charts for a web dashboard instead of static PNGs?

Yes; instruct the agent to output a Vega-Lite or Plotly JSON specification populated with the aggregated result dictionary, which your React frontend renders interactively without executing arbitrary JavaScript.

### How do I handle missing values (`NaN`) before running statistical correlations?

Report the exact null_count per column in the profile and explicitly log whether rows with NaN were dropped (dropna()) or imputed (fillna(median)) in the cleaning_actions audit trail.

body:
## Introduction

To build an AI browser agent that reliably navigates dynamic websites, fills multi-step forms, and executes workflows without breaking whenever a CSS class name changes, you must combine DOM Accessibility Tree indexing with visual Set-of-Marks (SoM) screenshot grounding and mandatory human approval gates for state-mutating actions. Traditional Selenium or Playwright scripts hardcode brittle XPath or CSS selectors (div.btn-primary-v2 > span) that break on every frontend deployment. Conversely, sending a raw 5MB HTML string to an LLM overflows the context window. By injecting a lightweight JavaScript script that assigns sequential numeric IDs ([1], [2], [3]) to visible, interactive DOM elements (<button>, <input>, <a>, <select>) and pairing them with Playwright for Python (https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-python) or Browser-Use (https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use), your agent can navigate complex web applications using compact numeric element indices.

> [!TIP]
> **Architecture Reference:** Internal Link Suggestion: For read-only web research and report synthesis, see [Article 1: How to Build an AI Research Agent That Searches the Web and Writes Reports ](/writing/build-ai-research-agent-web-search-reports/).

## Browser Automation Architecture: DOM Indexing, Grounding & Action Safety

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Goal([User Task Goal]) --> Browser[Playwright Chromium Context]
    Browser --> DOMIndexer[JS Interactive Element Indexer + Accessibility Tree]
    DOMIndexer --> StateView[Compact Indexed Element List + Optional Screenshot]
    StateView --> Planner[LLM Action Planner: Click, Type, Select, Scroll, Done]
    Planner --> SafetyGate{Is Action High-Risk? Checkout / Delete / Submit}
    SafetyGate -- "Yes: High-Risk Action" --> HumanApprove[Pause for Human Confirmation]
    SafetyGate -- "No: Safe Navigation/Input" --> Executor[Playwright Action Executor]
    HumanApprove -- "Approved" --> Executor
    Executor --> Wait[Wait for Network Idle / DOM Settled]
    Wait --> DOMIndexer
```

### DOM Understanding vs. Screenshot-Based Interaction

1. Indexed DOM Extraction (Fast, Low Token Cost): A JavaScript snippet queries all interactive elements (button, a, input, select, textarea, [role="button"]), filters out elements with width == 0, height == 0, or visibility == "hidden", assigns a data-ai-id="12" attribute, and returns a clean list: [12] <input type="text" placeholder="Search flights...">.
1. Visual Set-of-Marks (Fallback for Canvas & Custom Widgets): When a site renders controls inside custom <canvas> elements or unlabeled <div> tags, overlay numbered bounding boxes onto a viewport screenshot and pass both the image and the DOM index list to a multimodal model.

## Technology Comparison: Paid vs. Open-Source Stack

*(Verified October 30, 2026 via browser-use/browser-use (https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use) and microsoft/playwright-python (https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-python)).*

| Component | Commercial / Hosted Solution | Open-Source Alternative | Self-Hosting Possible? | Technical & Pricing Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Browser Agent Framework | Browser Use Cloud API / MultiOn | Browser-Use (https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use) (MIT License, v0.13.14, 119.6k stars) | Yes (Python >= 3.11) | Supports local Chromium, CDP connections, and deterministic action replay (load_and_rerun). |
| Browser Automation Driver | Browserbase / Browser Use Cloud (\$0.02/browser-hr) | Playwright for Python (https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-python) (Apache-2.0, v1.64.1) | Yes | Built-in auto-waiting and real mouse/keyboard event dispatch across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. |
| Action Planning LLM | OpenAI (gpt-4o / gpt-4.1) / Claude Sonnet | Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (Qwen2.5-VL-32B / Llama-3.3-70B) | Yes | Vision-language models require \~1,000 image tokens per viewport screenshot. |

### Recommended Implementation Options

### Option A: Best Practical Implementation (Recommended): Python 3.12 + Browser-Use (https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use) or custom Playwright (https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-python) DOM indexer + OpenAI/Claude structured action loop + human approval middleware for form submissions.

### Option B: Fully Open-Source Local Implementation: Browser-Use (https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use) + local Chromium + Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (qwen2.5:32b).

### Option C: Production Cloud Browser Pool: Python agent connected over Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) to Browser Use Cloud (https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use) (\$0.02/hour stealth browsers with profile sync and session recordings).

## Step-by-Step Implementation Guide

### Step 1: Project Structure

```text
ai-browser-agent/
├── app/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── dom_indexer.py
│   ├── schemas.py
│   └── navigator.py
├── tests/
│   └── test_browser_agent.py
└── requirements.txt
```

### Step 2: Implement the Interactive DOM Element Indexer (app/dom_indexer.py)

Rather than sending raw HTML to the LLM, this parser extracts only visible interactive controls and assigns deterministic integer indices ([1], [2], ...) mapped to unique CSS selectors:

```python
from typing import List, Dict
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from pydantic import BaseModel

INTERACTIVE_TAGS = {"a", "button", "input", "select", "textarea"}

class IndexedElement(BaseModel):
    index: int
    tag: str
    element_type: str
    text_or_label: str
    selector: str
    is_sensitive_submit: bool = False

SENSITIVE_KEYWORDS = ("pay", "purchase", "buy now", "checkout", "delete", "transfer", "confirm order", "wire")

def index_interactive_dom_from_html(html: str) -> List[IndexedElement]:
    """Parses HTML and assigns sequential 1-based indices to interactive elements."""
    soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser")
    elements: List[IndexedElement] = []
    idx = 1

    for tag in soup.find_all(lambda t: t.name in INTERACTIVE_TAGS or t.get("role") == "button"):
        if tag.get("type") == "hidden" or "display:none" in str(tag.get("style", "")).replace(" ", "").lower():
            continue

        el_type = str(tag.get("type", tag.name))
        label = (
            tag.get_text(strip=True)
            or str(tag.get("placeholder", ""))
            or str(tag.get("aria-label", ""))
            or str(tag.get("name", ""))
            or str(tag.get("value", ""))
        )[:80]

        el_id = tag.get("id")
        el_name = tag.get("name")
        if el_id:
            selector = f"#{el_id}"
        elif el_name:
            selector = f"{tag.name}[name='{el_name}']"
        else:
            selector = f"{tag.name}:nth-of-type({idx})"

        combined_text = f"{label} {el_id or ''} {el_name or ''}".lower()
        is_sensitive = any(k in combined_text for k in SENSITIVE_KEYWORDS)

        elements.append(
            IndexedElement(
                index=idx,
                tag=tag.name,
                element_type=el_type,
                text_or_label=label,
                selector=selector,
                is_sensitive_submit=is_sensitive,
            )
        )
        idx += 1

    return elements

def format_indexed_dom_for_llm(elements: List[IndexedElement]) -> str:
    """Formats the interactive element map into a compact token representation for the LLM."""
    lines = []
    for el in elements:
        flag = " [SENSITIVE_ACTION_REQUIRES_APPROVAL]" if el.is_sensitive_submit else ""
        lines.append(f"[{el.index}] <{el.tag} type='{el.element_type}'> \"{el.text_or_label}\"{flag}")
    return "\n".join(lines)
```

### Step 3: Define Browser Action Schemas and Human Approval Gate (app/schemas.py & app/navigator.py)

```python
from enum import Enum
from typing import Optional, List
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from app.dom_indexer import IndexedElement

class ActionType(str, Enum):
    CLICK = "CLICK"
    FILL_TEXT = "FILL_TEXT"
    GOTO_URL = "GOTO_URL"
    ASK_HUMAN_APPROVAL = "ASK_HUMAN_APPROVAL"
    COMPLETE = "COMPLETE"

class BrowserStepAction(BaseModel):
    action_type: ActionType
    target_element_index: Optional[int] = Field(None, ge=1)
    text_input: Optional[str] = None
    reasoning: str

def verify_action_safety(
    action: BrowserStepAction,
    indexed_elements: List[IndexedElement],
    human_approved: bool = False,
) -> BrowserStepAction:
    """Intercepts clicks on sensitive checkout/delete/payment buttons if human_approved is False."""
    if action.action_type == ActionType.CLICK and action.target_element_index is not None:
        matched = next((e for e in indexed_elements if e.index == action.target_element_index), None)
        if matched is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Element index [{action.target_element_index}] does not exist on page.")
        if matched.is_sensitive_submit and not human_approved:
            return BrowserStepAction(
                action_type=ActionType.ASK_HUMAN_APPROVAL,
                target_element_index=matched.index,
                reasoning=f"Intercepted sensitive action on [{matched.index}] '{matched.text_or_label}'. Waiting for human confirmation.",
            )
    return action
```

## Testing the Browser Agent (tests/test_browser_agent.py)

```python
from app.dom_indexer import index_interactive_dom_from_html, format_indexed_dom_for_llm
from app.schemas import BrowserStepAction, ActionType, verify_action_safety

SAMPLE_CHECKOUT_HTML = """
<html>
  <body>
    <input id="search-box" type="text" placeholder="Search products" />
    <input id="csrf-token" type="hidden" value="secret123" />
    <button id="filter-btn">Apply Filter</button>
    <button id="pay-btn">Pay Now $499</button>
  </body>
</html>
"""

def test_dom_indexer_skips_hidden_inputs_and_flags_sensitive_buttons():
    elements = index_interactive_dom_from_html(SAMPLE_CHECKOUT_HTML)
    assert len(elements) == 3  # hidden input skipped
    assert elements[0].selector == "#search-box"
    assert elements[1].is_sensitive_submit is False
    assert elements[2].text_or_label == "Pay Now $499"
    assert elements[2].is_sensitive_submit is True

    prompt_view = format_indexed_dom_for_llm(elements)
    assert "[3] <button type='button'> \"Pay Now $499\" [SENSITIVE_ACTION_REQUIRES_APPROVAL]" in prompt_view

def test_safety_gate_intercepts_unapproved_payment_click():
    elements = index_interactive_dom_from_html(SAMPLE_CHECKOUT_HTML)
    proposed_click = BrowserStepAction(
        action_type=ActionType.CLICK,
        target_element_index=3,
        reasoning="Click the Pay Now button to complete purchase.",
    )
    gated = verify_action_safety(proposed_click, elements, human_approved=False)
    assert gated.action_type == ActionType.ASK_HUMAN_APPROVAL

    approved = verify_action_safety(proposed_click, elements, human_approved=True)
    assert approved.action_type == ActionType.CLICK
```

## Authentication, Session Security & Cost Considerations

- Handling Authentication Safely: Never hardcode plaintext passwords into LLM prompts (where they leak into model provider logs or trace snapshots). In Browser-Use (https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use), pass credentials via the sensitive_data={"x_password": "..."} dictionary so the LLM only sees placeholder tokens (<secret>x_password</secret>), or authenticate once in a persistent Playwright browser context (storage_state="auth_state.json") and reuse session cookies.
- Zero-LLM Replay for Recurring Tasks: As documented in Browser-Use v0.13.14 (https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use), once an agent completes a workflow (such as downloading a monthly vendor invoice), save the run history (agent.save_history("run.json")) and replay it with new variables (load_and_rerun) without calling the LLM on every click.

## Useful Tools, Documentation and GitHub Repositories

| Resource | Purpose | Type | Link |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Browser-Use | Open-source AI browser agent library & cloud stealth browsers | Open-Source (MIT) | https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use |
| Playwright for Python | Deterministic cross-browser automation engine | Open-Source (Apache-2.0) | https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-python |
| Playwright Docs | Official Python async API and locator documentation | Documentation | https://playwright.dev/python/docs/intro |

## Frequently Asked Questions

### When should I use raw Playwright vs. an AI browser agent like Browser-Use?

Use deterministic Playwright scripts when automating a single known website that you control (such as your own E2E test suite). Use an AI browser agent when navigating dozens of external vendor portals whose DOM structures vary or change unpredictably.

### How do I prevent an AI browser agent from making accidental purchases or deleting data?

Classify every button or form submission against sensitive keywords (pay, checkout, delete, wire, remove) and HTTP methods (POST/DELETE to billing endpoints) in deterministic middleware (verify_action_safety), pausing execution until the user approves the action.

### Why shouldn't I put user passwords inside the browser agent prompt?

Anything placed in the prompt is sent to the LLM API and saved in execution trace logs. Inject credentials via Playwright storage state cookies or sensitive_data secret placeholders.

### How do I handle Single-Page Applications (React/Next.js) that load content asynchronously?

After every click or navigation action, wait for network activity to settle (await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")) and re-run the DOM indexer before planning the next step.

### How much does it cost to run a cloud stealth browser in production?

Per Browser-Use official pricing (https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use) (checked October 30, 2026), cloud stealth browsers cost \$0.02 per browser-hour plus network traffic, or \$0 if running headless Chromium on your own server.

### Can I rerun a successful browser workflow without paying for LLM tokens on every step?

Yes; record the action trajectory (save_history) and replay parameterized form fills deterministically, invoking the LLM only if a selector fails due to a site redesign.

### How do I defend against prompt injection hidden inside a webpage's text?

Restrict the action planner's view to the structured interactive element list (format_indexed_dom_for_llm) when navigating, and prohibit the agent from navigating to arbitrary external domains outside the task's allowlisted domain scope.

### What happens if an element is inside an `<iframe>` or Shadow DOM?

Use Playwright's page.frames and built-in shadow-piercing locators to traverse open shadow roots when building the interactive element map.

faqItems.question: Why does OpenAlex return `abstract_inverted_index` instead of a plain string?
faqItems.answer: To comply with publisher copyright restrictions while enabling open text mining, OpenAlex stores abstracts as word-position inverted indices. Our reconstruct_inverted_abstract() helper restores the exact readable abstract in $O(N \log N)$ time.

faqItems.question: How do I access OpenAlex's fast "Polite Pool"?
faqItems.answer: Pass your contact email in the query parameters (?mailto=you@domain.com) or User-Agent header. OpenAlex routes polite requests to dedicated low-latency servers supporting up to 100,000 requests per day for free.

faqItems.question: How do I check if a scientific paper has been retracted?
faqItems.answer: Check the is_retracted boolean field on the OpenAlex Work object (item.get("is_retracted")) or the update-to array in Crossref metadata, and automatically exclude retracted works from synthesis.

faqItems.question: How do I compare experimental results across papers fairly?
faqItems.answer: Extract a structured PaperMethodologyComparison table capturing the exact benchmark dataset (datasets_evaluated), evaluation metric (F1, RMSE, AUC), and baseline model so the synthesizer never compares metrics evaluated on different datasets.

faqItems.question: Can this assistant download full-text PDFs legally?
faqItems.answer: Yes, when open_access.is_oa is True in OpenAlex or openAccessPdf is present in Semantic Scholar (such as arXiv, PubMed Central, and CC-BY journals). Never bypass publisher paywalls.

faqItems.question: How do I discover seminal older papers that use different terminology than my search query?
faqItems.answer: Run 1-hop backward and forward citation snowballing: inspect the referenced_works array of your top 5 search hits to find the foundational papers cited by all of them.

faqItems.question: How do I parse two-column IEEE or ACM PDFs without jumbling equations and tables?
faqItems.answer: Use Docling (https://github.com/docling-project/docling), which runs a layout detection model to segment columns, figures, and tables before extracting Markdown.

faqItems.question: Can I run this academic assistant locally for unpublished lab manuscripts?
faqItems.answer: Yes; pair local Docling (https://github.com/docling-project/docling) PDF extraction with Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) so unpublished grant proposals and manuscripts remain 100% on-premise.

body:
## Introduction

To build an AI academic research assistant that discovers peer-reviewed literature, maps citation graphs, compares experimental methodologies, and synthesises literature reviews without fabricating citations, you must query authoritative scholarly metadata graphs—specifically **OpenAlex** (https://openalex.org/), **Semantic Scholar** (https://www.semanticscholar.org/product/api), Crossref, and arXiv—and anchor every claim to a verified Digital Object Identifier (DOI) or arXiv ID. Generic web search engines struggle to return structured citation networks, inverted abstract indices, or retraction flags, and asking an LLM to generate a bibliography from memory guarantees hallucinated author-year-journal combinations.

> [!TIP]
> **Architecture Reference:** Internal Link Suggestion: On Aniket.app (https://aniket.app/), see the [OIST Applied AI Research](/research/) section detailing automated scientific literature ingestion pipelines that synthesize unstructured publications into structured datasets, and cross-reference [Article 1: How to Build an AI Research Agent ](/writing/build-ai-research-agent-web-search-reports/).

## Scholarly Discovery, Citation Graph & Synthesis Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Query([Research Hypothesis / Literature Topic]) --> FederatedSearch[Federated API Query: OpenAlex + Semantic Scholar + arXiv]
    FederatedSearch --> Dedupe[DOI & Title Deduplicator + Retraction Filter]
    Dedupe --> CitationGraph[Snowball Citation Expander: Forward & Backward References]
    CitationGraph --> PDFExtract[Full-Text PDF Parser: Docling Methodology & Results Tables]
    PDFExtract --> Matrix[Structured Comparison Matrix: Dataset, Metric, Baseline, Limitations]
    Matrix --> BibVerifier[Deterministic DOI / BibTeX Citation Validator]
    BibVerifier --> Review([Reproducible Literature Review + Verified BibTeX])
```

### How OpenAlex Inverted Abstracts and Citation Graphs Work

1. **OpenAlex API** (https://openalex.org/) (CC0 Public Domain, 500M+ Works): To save storage bandwidth, OpenAlex returns paper abstracts as an abstract_inverted_index JSON dictionary mapping each word to its list of integer token positions ({"Graph": [0], "neural": [1], "networks": [2]}). Your ingestion client must reconstruct the plaintext abstract deterministically by sorting word-position pairs.
1. **Semantic Scholar Academic Graph API** (https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/): Provides citationCount, influentialCitationCount, openAccessPdf, tldr, and SPECTER2 paper embeddings for semantic similarity discovery.
1. Crossref REST API (`api.crossref.org/works/{doi}`): Serves as the authoritative registry for verifying whether a DOI exists, checking publication dates, and detecting is-retracted update notices.

## Technology Comparison: Paid vs. Open-Source Scholarly Stack

| Component | Commercial / Subscription Database | Open-Source / Open-Data Alternative | Self-Hosting / Free Tier? | Technical & Rate-Limit Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Scholarly Index & Metadata | Scopus / Web of Science / Dimensions | OpenAlex (https://openalex.org/) (CC0 License) + Crossref (Open Metadata) | Yes (100% Free Polite Pool: 100k req/day with mailto:) | OpenAlex requires reconstructing abstract_inverted_index into text. |
| Citation Graph & Embeddings | Connected Papers Pro / Scite.ai | Semantic Scholar API (https://www.semanticscholar.org/product/api) + arXiv API | Free API tier available | Semantic Scholar caps unauthenticated requests; pass x-api-key and respect per-second rate limits. |
| Scientific PDF & Equation Parser | Mathpix Snipping API | Docling (https://github.com/docling-project/docling) (MIT) / pypdf | Yes | Multi-column LaTeX PDFs require layout-aware reading order so equations and result tables stay intact. |
| Synthesis LLM | OpenAI (gpt-4.1) / Claude Sonnet | Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (Qwen2.5-32B / DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B) | Yes | Must extract exact sample sizes ($N$), evaluation metrics, and baselines without extrapolating. |

### Recommended Implementation Options

### Option A: Best Practical Implementation (Recommended): Python 3.12 + httpx async federated client for OpenAlex (https://openalex.org/) & Semantic Scholar (https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/) + Docling (https://github.com/docling-project/docling) for open-access PDF table parsing + OpenAI/Claude structured methodology extraction + deterministic BibTeX generator.

### Option B: Fully Open-Source Implementation: OpenAlex + arXiv API + Docling (https://github.com/docling-project/docling) + local Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (qwen2.5:32b) + pgvector (https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector).

### Option C: Production Institutional Research Pipeline: Local OpenAlex snapshot / PostgreSQL graph + automated arXiv daily category poller (cs.AI, cs.LG, q-fin) + vector similarity alert engine.

## Step-by-Step Implementation Guide

### Step 1: Project Structure

```text
ai-academic-assistant/
├── app/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── openalex_client.py
│   ├── schemas.py
│   └── bibtex_verifier.py
├── tests/
│   └── test_academic_assistant.py
└── requirements.txt
```

### Step 2: Implement the OpenAlex Inverted Abstract Reconstructor & Search Client (app/openalex_client.py)

```python
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any
import httpx
from pydantic import BaseModel

class ScholarlyPaper(BaseModel):
    work_id: str
    doi: Optional[str]
    title: str
    publication_year: int
    authors: List[str]
    venue: str
    cited_by_count: int
    abstract_text: str
    open_access_pdf_url: Optional[str] = None

def reconstruct_inverted_abstract(inverted_index: Optional[Dict[str, List[int]]]) -> str:
    """Deterministically reconstructs plaintext abstract from OpenAlex abstract_inverted_index."""
    if not inverted_index:
        return ""
    position_map: Dict[int, str] = {}
    for word, positions in inverted_index.items():
        for pos in positions:
            position_map[pos] = word
    if not position_map:
        return ""
    sorted_indices = sorted(position_map.keys())
    return " ".join(position_map[i] for i in sorted_indices)

async def search_openalex_works(
    query: str,
    polite_email: str,
    max_results: int = 5,
    min_year: int = 2020,
) -> List[ScholarlyPaper]:
    """Queries OpenAlex /works API using the polite pool (mailto parameter)."""
    params = {
        "search": query,
        "filter": f"publication_year:>={min_year}",
        "per-page": max_results,
        "mailto": polite_email,
    }
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=15.0) as client:
        resp = await client.get("https://api.openalex.org/works", params=params)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        data = resp.json()

    papers: List[ScholarlyPaper] = []
    for item in data.get("results", []):
        authors = [
            a.get("author", {}).get("display_name", "Unknown")
            for a in item.get("authorships", [])[:6]
        ]
        primary_loc = item.get("primary_location") or {}
        source_info = primary_loc.get("source") or {}
        venue_name = source_info.get("display_name") or "Preprint / Unknown Venue"
        oa_info = item.get("open_access") or {}

        papers.append(
            ScholarlyPaper(
                work_id=item.get("id", ""),
                doi=item.get("doi"),
                title=item.get("title") or "Untitled",
                publication_year=int(item.get("publication_year") or 0),
                authors=authors,
                venue=venue_name,
                cited_by_count=int(item.get("cited_by_count") or 0),
                abstract_text=reconstruct_inverted_abstract(item.get("abstract_inverted_index")),
                open_access_pdf_url=oa_info.get("oa_url"),
            )
        )
    return papers
```

### Step 3: Implement Methodology Comparison Schemas & Deterministic BibTeX Generation (app/schemas.py & app/bibtex_verifier.py)

```python
import re
from typing import List, Dict
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from app.openalex_client import ScholarlyPaper

class PaperMethodologyComparison(BaseModel):
    work_id: str
    doi: str
    core_methodology: str = Field(..., description="Architecture or statistical method used.")
    datasets_evaluated: List[str]
    primary_quantitative_result: str = Field(..., description="Exact metric and value reported, e.g. 'F1 = 89.4% on SciERC'")
    stated_limitations: str

def generate_verified_bibtex(paper: ScholarlyPaper) -> str:
    """Generates a deterministic BibTeX entry strictly from verified OpenAlex/Crossref metadata."""
    first_author_last = paper.authors[0].split()[-1].lower() if paper.authors else "unknown"
    clean_author = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", first_author_last)
    cite_key = f"{clean_author}{paper.publication_year}"
    author_str = " and ".join(paper.authors) if paper.authors else "Unknown"
    doi_line = f"  doi = {{{paper.doi}}},\n" if paper.doi else ""

    return (
        f"@article{{{cite_key},\n"
        f"  title = {{{paper.title}}},\n"
        f"  author = {{{author_str}}},\n"
        f"  journal = {{{paper.venue}}},\n"
        f"  year = {{{paper.publication_year}}},\n"
        f"{doi_line}"
        f"}}"
    )

def verify_inline_doi_citations(review_markdown: str, verified_papers: Dict[str, ScholarlyPaper]) -> List[str]:
    """Checks that every cited DOI or work_id in the literature review exists in the retrieved paper registry."""
    cited_dois = re.findall(r"https://doi\.org/[^\s\)\]]+", review_markdown)
    known_dois = {p.doi for p in verified_papers.values() if p.doi}
    unverified = [d for d in cited_dois if d not in known_dois]
    return unverified
```

```python
from app.openalex_client import reconstruct_inverted_abstract, ScholarlyPaper
from app.bibtex_verifier import generate_verified_bibtex, verify_inline_doi_citations

def test_reconstruct_openalex_inverted_abstract():
    inv = {
        "Graph": [0],
        "neural": [1],
        "networks": [2, 6],
        "model": [3],
        "ecological": [4],
        "food": [5],
    }
    text = reconstruct_inverted_abstract(inv)
    assert text == "Graph neural networks model ecological food networks"

def test_verified_bibtex_and_doi_checker():
    paper = ScholarlyPaper(
        work_id="https://openalex.org/W123",
        doi="https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-00001-x",
        title="Topological Learning in Trophic Networks",
        publication_year=2025,
        authors=["Aniket Thakur", "Kenji Sato"],
        venue="Nature Machine Intelligence",
        cited_by_count=42,
        abstract_text="We introduce an attention-based GNN...",
    )
    bibtex = generate_verified_bibtex(paper)
    assert "@article{thakur2025," in bibtex
    assert "doi = {https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-00001-x}" in bibtex

    registry = {paper.work_id: paper}
    review = (
        "Recent work ([Thakur & Sato, 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-00001-x)) "
        "and a hallucinated citation ([Fake, 2024](https://doi.org/10.9999/fake.123))."
    )
    unverified = verify_inline_doi_citations(review, registry)
    assert unverified == ["https://doi.org/10.9999/fake.123"]
```

## Source Verification, Reproducibility & Cost Considerations

- Never Let the LLM Write BibTeX from Scratch: LLMs frequently swap volume and issue numbers or invent page ranges when formatting BibTeX. Always generate .bib entries deterministically from the JSON metadata returned by OpenAlex (https://openalex.org/), Semantic Scholar (https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/), or Crossref (generate_verified_bibtex).
- Cost Breakdown: OpenAlex, Crossref, and arXiv APIs are 100% free. Synthesising a 30-paper systematic literature review costs \~\$0.05–$0.15 per review in LLM tokens or \$0 with local Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama).

## Useful Tools, Documentation and GitHub Repositories

| Resource | Purpose | Type | Link |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAlex | Free CC0 global catalog of 500M+ scholarly works | Open Data / API | https://openalex.org/ |
| Semantic Scholar API | Citation graphs, SPECTER2 embeddings, and paper TLDRs | Official API Docs | https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/ |
| Docling | Multi-column scientific PDF and table extraction | Open-Source (MIT) | https://github.com/docling-project/docling |

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why does OpenAlex return `abstract_inverted_index` instead of a plain string?

To comply with publisher copyright restrictions while enabling open text mining, OpenAlex stores abstracts as word-position inverted indices. Our reconstruct_inverted_abstract() helper restores the exact readable abstract in $O(N \log N)$ time.

### How do I access OpenAlex's fast "Polite Pool"?

Pass your contact email in the query parameters (?mailto=you@domain.com) or User-Agent header. OpenAlex routes polite requests to dedicated low-latency servers supporting up to 100,000 requests per day for free.

### How do I check if a scientific paper has been retracted?

Check the is_retracted boolean field on the OpenAlex Work object (item.get("is_retracted")) or the update-to array in Crossref metadata, and automatically exclude retracted works from synthesis.

### How do I compare experimental results across papers fairly?

Extract a structured PaperMethodologyComparison table capturing the exact benchmark dataset (datasets_evaluated), evaluation metric (F1, RMSE, AUC), and baseline model so the synthesizer never compares metrics evaluated on different datasets.

### Can this assistant download full-text PDFs legally?

Yes, when open_access.is_oa is True in OpenAlex or openAccessPdf is present in Semantic Scholar (such as arXiv, PubMed Central, and CC-BY journals). Never bypass publisher paywalls.

### How do I discover seminal older papers that use different terminology than my search query?

Run 1-hop backward and forward citation snowballing: inspect the referenced_works array of your top 5 search hits to find the foundational papers cited by all of them.

### How do I parse two-column IEEE or ACM PDFs without jumbling equations and tables?

Use Docling (https://github.com/docling-project/docling), which runs a layout detection model to segment columns, figures, and tables before extracting Markdown.

### Can I run this academic assistant locally for unpublished lab manuscripts?

Yes; pair local Docling (https://github.com/docling-project/docling) PDF extraction with Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) so unpublished grant proposals and manuscripts remain 100% on-premise.
