body:
## Introduction

To build a multilingual AI voice assistant for Indian users who naturally blend Hindi and English within the same sentence (Hinglish code-switching, e.g., *"Mera order status check karo aur delivery address update karna hai"*), you cannot force the user to select a rigid "Hindi" or "English" language toggle at the start of the conversation. Standard monolingual ASR models garble English technical nouns (*"EMI"*, *"refund"*, *"account statement"*) when forced into pure Hindi mode, or transcribe Hindi verbs as nonsense English homophones when locked to en-US. To build a fluent Hindi-English voice assistant, you must configure code-switch-aware multilingual Speech Recognition, Devanagari/Roman script and numeric normalisation, bilingual system prompt grounding, and Indic-accent neural Text-to-Speech.

> [!TIP]
> **Architecture Reference:** Internal Link Suggestion: Combine this bilingual pipeline with [Article 17: How to Build an AI Phone Receptionist and [Article 19: How to Build a Real-Time AI Translation System ](/writing/build-ai-phone-receptionist-twilio-voice-calls/](/writing/build-real-time-ai-translation-voice-conversations/)).

## Bilingual & Code-Switching Voice Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Audio([User Speech: Hindi / English / Hinglish]) --> VAD[Silero VAD Endpointing]
    VAD --> ASR[Multilingual ASR: Deepgram Nova-3 Multi / Faster-Whisper large-v3]
    ASR --> Normalizer[Hinglish & Devanagari Normaliser + Keyterm Booster]
    Normalizer --> LangDetect[Utterance Script & Language Ratio Detector]
    LangDetect --> LLM[Bilingual LLM: Replies Matching User's Language/Register]
    LLM --> TTSRouter{Select TTS Voice Profile}
    TTSRouter -- "Devanagari / Hindi Dominant" --> HindiTTS[Hindi/Indic Neural TTS]
    TTSRouter -- "English / Hinglish Conversational" --> BilingualTTS[Multilingual Indian-Accent TTS]
```

### Solving Code-Switching and Indian Accent Challenges

1. Never Force `language="en"` on Code-Switched Audio: In Deepgram Nova-3 (https://deepgram.com/pricing), set language="multi" (\$0.0092/min on Pay-as-you-go). In Faster-Whisper (https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) (large-v3 or turbo), leave language=None (or provide a bilingual initial_prompt containing both Devanagari and English domain terms: "नमस्ते, मेरा order status और payment receipt check कीजिए।"). That bilingual initial_prompt primes Whisper's decoder to emit Devanagari for Hindi words and Latin script for English technical terms rather than transliterating everything phonetically.
1. Script & Number Normalisation before TTS: If the LLM outputs "आपका रिफंड ₹1,250.00 कल तक आ जाएगा", verify that your TTS engine expands ₹1,250 naturally; otherwise normalise currency symbols and abbreviations in Python before synthesis.

#### Evaluating Transcription Quality (WER & CER): Because Hinglish utterances often mix scripts (e.g., "मेरा order" vs "मेरा आर्डर"), standard case-sensitive Word Error Rate (WER) over-penalises valid transcriptions. Always normalise Unicode (NFKC), strip punctuation, and compute both Word Error Rate (WER) and Character Error Rate (CER).

## Technology Comparison: Paid vs. Open-Source Multilingual Stack

| Component | Commercial API | Open-Source / Open-Weight Alternative | Self-Hosting Possible? | Hindi/Hinglish Technical Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Multilingual Speech-to-Text | Deepgram Nova-3 Multilingual (https://deepgram.com/pricing) (\$0.0092/min) / Sarvam AI / Google Chirp | Faster-Whisper (https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) (large-v3, MIT) / AI4Bharat IndicConformer / IndicWhisper (MIT) | Yes | AI4Bharat's Indic models achieve low WER on regional Indian accents; Whisper large-v3 with a bilingual initial_prompt handles Hinglish code-switching well. |
| Bilingual LLM | OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini / gpt-4.1) / Gemini | Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (Gemma 4 / Qwen2.5-32B / Llama-3.3-70B) | Yes | Instruct the LLM to mirror the user's language mix (pure Hindi, conversational Hinglish, or English). |
| Hindi & Indian-English TTS | Cartesia Sonic Multilingual / ElevenLabs / Azure hi-IN-SwaraNeural | AI4Bharat Indic-Parler-TTS (Apache-2.0) / OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl (https://github.com/OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl) (hi_IN voices) | Yes | Ensure TTS supports both Devanagari (\u0900-\u097F) and embedded English words. |

### Recommended Implementation Options

### Option A: Best Practical Implementation (Recommended): LiveKit Agents (https://github.com/livekit/agents) + Deepgram Nova-3 (language="multi") + gpt-4o-mini (or Gemma 4) + Cartesia/Indic-accent multilingual TTS.

### Option B: Fully Open-Source Self-Hosted Stack: Faster-Whisper (https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) (large-v3) or AI4Bharat IndicWhisper + local Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (gemma4) + AI4Bharat Indic-Parler-TTS.

### Option C: Production Enterprise Contact Center (India): Pipecat (https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat) + regional telephony serializer (Exotel/Plivo/Twilio) + streaming bilingual STT/TTS + WER evaluation harness.

## Step-by-Step Implementation Guide

### Step 1: Project Structure

```text
multilingual-voice-assistant/
├── app/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── hinglish_normalizer.py
│   └── wer_evaluator.py
├── tests/
│   └── test_multilingual_assistant.py
└── requirements.txt
```

### Step 2: Implement Script Detection, Bilingual Prompting & TTS Text Normaliser (app/hinglish_normalizer.py)

```python
import re
import unicodedata
from enum import Enum
from pydantic import BaseModel

DEVANAGARI_RANGE = re.compile(r"[\u0900-\u097F]")
LATIN_WORD_RANGE = re.compile(r"[a-zA-Z]+")
COMMON_ROMAN_HINDI_TOKENS = {
    "mera", "meri", "kya", "hai", "nahi", "karo", "karna", "kab",
    "aayega", "paisa", "bhaiya", "kripya", "batao", "mujhe", "chahiye",
}

class UtteranceLanguageMode(str, Enum):
    HINDI_DEVANAGARI = "HINDI_DEVANAGARI"
    HINGLISH_CODE_SWITCH = "HINGLISH_CODE_SWITCH"
    ENGLISH_INDIAN = "ENGLISH_INDIAN"

class LanguageAnalysis(BaseModel):
    mode: UtteranceLanguageMode
    devanagari_char_count: int
    latin_word_count: int
    normalized_tts_text: str

def detect_and_normalize_utterance(text: str) -> LanguageAnalysis:
    """Detects Hindi/English/Hinglish mode and normalizes symbols for clean TTS pronunciation."""
    norm = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text).strip()
    dev_chars = len(DEVANAGARI_RANGE.findall(norm))
    latin_words = [w.lower() for w in LATIN_WORD_RANGE.findall(norm)]
    roman_hindi_hits = sum(1 for w in latin_words if w in COMMON_ROMAN_HINDI_TOKENS)

    if dev_chars > 0 and len(latin_words) > 0:
        mode = UtteranceLanguageMode.HINGLISH_CODE_SWITCH
    elif dev_chars > 0:
        mode = UtteranceLanguageMode.HINDI_DEVANAGARI
    elif roman_hindi_hits >= 1:
        mode = UtteranceLanguageMode.HINGLISH_CODE_SWITCH
    else:
        mode = UtteranceLanguageMode.ENGLISH_INDIAN

    # Expand ₹ currency symbol so TTS reads it naturally in the target register
    if mode in (UtteranceLanguageMode.HINDI_DEVANAGARI, UtteranceLanguageMode.HINGLISH_CODE_SWITCH):
        tts_text = re.sub(r"₹\s*([0-9,]+)", r"\1 रुपये", norm)
    else:
        tts_text = re.sub(r"₹\s*([0-9,]+)", r"\1 rupees", norm)

    return LanguageAnalysis(
        mode=mode,
        devanagari_char_count=dev_chars,
        latin_word_count=len(latin_words),
        normalized_tts_text=tts_text,
    )
```

### Step 3: Implement Dynamic Programming Word Error Rate (WER) & CER Evaluator (app/wer_evaluator.py)

To benchmark Whisper vs. Deepgram vs. IndicConformer on your own Hindi-English audio test set, use exact Levenshtein edit distance at both word and character levels:

```python
import re
import unicodedata
from typing import List

def normalize_for_asr_eval(text: str) -> str:
    """Normalizes Unicode, lowercases Latin characters, and strips punctuation for fair WER/CER."""
    norm = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text).lower()
    norm = re.sub(r"[^\w\s\u0900-\u097F]", "", norm)
    return " ".join(norm.split())

def _edit_distance(ref_seq: List[str], hyp_seq: List[str]) -> int:
    n, m = len(ref_seq), len(hyp_seq)
    dp = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(n + 1):
        dp[i][0] = i
    for j in range(m + 1):
        dp[0][j] = j
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            cost = 0 if ref_seq[i - 1] == hyp_seq[j - 1] else 1
            dp[i][j] = min(
                dp[i - 1][j] + 1,      # deletion
                dp[i][j - 1] + 1,      # insertion
                dp[i - 1][j - 1] + cost # substitution
            )
    return dp[n][m]

def compute_wer_and_cer(reference: str, hypothesis: str) -> dict:
    """Computes normalized Word Error Rate (WER) and Character Error Rate (CER)."""
    clean_ref = normalize_for_asr_eval(reference)
    clean_hyp = normalize_for_asr_eval(hypothesis)

    ref_words = clean_ref.split()
    hyp_words = clean_hyp.split()
    word_edits = _edit_distance(ref_words, hyp_words)
    wer = round(word_edits / max(1, len(ref_words)), 4)

    ref_chars = list(clean_ref.replace(" ", ""))
    hyp_chars = list(clean_hyp.replace(" ", ""))
    char_edits = _edit_distance(ref_chars, hyp_chars)
    cer = round(char_edits / max(1, len(ref_chars)), 4)

    return {"wer": wer, "cer": cer, "word_edits": word_edits, "ref_word_count": len(ref_words)}
```

## Testing the Multilingual Voice Assistant (tests/test_multilingual_assistant.py)

```python
from app.hinglish_normalizer import detect_and_normalize_utterance, UtteranceLanguageMode
from app.wer_evaluator import compute_wer_and_cer

def test_hinglish_detection_and_rupee_expansion():
    mixed = detect_and_normalize_utterance("मेरा refund ₹1,500 कब आएगा?")
    assert mixed.mode == UtteranceLanguageMode.HINGLISH_CODE_SWITCH
    assert "1,500 रुपये" in mixed.normalized_tts_text

    roman_hinglish = detect_and_normalize_utterance("Bhaiya mera order status kya hai?")
    assert roman_hinglish.mode == UtteranceLanguageMode.HINGLISH_CODE_SWITCH

    english = detect_and_normalize_utterance("Please send the invoice for ₹2,000.")
    assert english.mode == UtteranceLanguageMode.ENGLISH_INDIAN
    assert "2,000 rupees" in english.normalized_tts_text

def test_wer_and_cer_calculation_on_bilingual_transcript():
    ref = "नमस्ते मेरा order status बताइए"
    hyp = "नमस्ते मेरा order स्टेटस बताइए"
    metrics = compute_wer_and_cer(ref, hyp)
    assert metrics["wer"] == 0.2  # 1 word script difference out of 5 words
    assert metrics["cer"] < 0.35
```

## Cost Considerations & Production Tuning

- Cost Breakdown (Checked October 30, 2026 via [Deepgram Pricing](https://deepgram.com/pricing)): Deepgram Nova-3 Multilingual streaming STT costs \$0.0092/min (\$0.55/hour) on Pay-as-you-go or \$0.0078/min (\$0.47/hour) on Growth, while self-hosted Faster-Whisper (https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) (large-v3) or AI4Bharat IndicConformer has \$0 per-minute API cost.

| Resource | Purpose | Type | Link |

| Faster-Whisper | Multilingual Whisper inference supporting 90+ languages | Open-Source (MIT) | https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper |
| Pipecat | Real-time voice framework with Sarvam, Deepgram & Whisper plugins | Open-Source (BSD-2) | https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat |

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why does Whisper sometimes transcribe Hindi speech into Urdu (Perso-Arabic) script instead of Devanagari?

Because spoken conversational Hindi and Urdu share similar phonology (Hindustani), Whisper's language token may pick ur if no script hint is provided. Passing a short Devanagari initial_prompt ("नमस्ते, आप कैसे हैं?") to model.transcribe(..., initial_prompt=...) anchors Whisper to Devanagari + Latin script without restricting vocabulary.

### How should the LLM respond when a user speaks Hinglish?

Instruct the LLM in the system prompt: *"Match the user's language register. If the user speaks conversational Hinglish, reply in natural conversational Hinglish using simple Hindi grammar with familiar English nouns (like 'order', 'payment', 'refund') rather than overly formal Sanskritised Hindi."*

### Why should I evaluate both Character Error Rate (CER) and Word Error Rate (WER) for Hindi?

In agglutinative or postpositional Indian languages and mixed-script Hinglish, a single matra (vowel sign) difference or compound word split ("ईमेल" vs "ई मेल") counts as a full 100% word error in WER even when 90% of characters are right. CER captures sub-word accuracy faithfully.

### How do I improve recognition of Indian proper nouns, city names, and brand names?

Use keyterm prompting in Deepgram Nova-3 (\$0.0013/min add-on) or pass domain vocabulary in Whisper's initial_prompt.

### Can [Pipecat](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat) connect directly to Indian telephony providers like Exotel or Plivo?

Yes! As verified in the Pipecat repository (https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat), Pipecat includes built-in transport serializers for Exotel, Plivo, Twilio, Telnyx, Genesys, and Vonage.

### What open-source TTS models support natural Hindi and Indian English?

AI4Bharat's Indic-Parler-TTS (Apache-2.0) generates natural Hindi and Indian-accented English speech with controllable speaker descriptions.

### How do I prevent the voice assistant from switching to Spanish or Welsh on short 1-second utterances like "Haan" or "Okay"?

Constrain automatic language detection to an allowlist of expected languages (["hi", "en"]) rather than letting the detector search across all 99 languages on a 0.5-second audio clip.

### How much VRAM is needed to self-host `faster-whisper` `large-v3` for Hindi-English?

Per Faster-Whisper's official benchmarks (https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper), large-v2/large-v3 with int8 quantization uses only \~2,926 MB to 4,500 MB of VRAM, fitting easily on an 8GB GPU.

faqItems.question: Why shouldn't I translate every word immediately as the STT model emits interim results?
faqItems.answer: Interim STT hypotheses change frequently as acoustic context arrives, and SOV/SVO languages invert verb positions. Translating unconfirmed interim tokens causes the TTS voice to repeat and contradict itself mid-sentence. Wait for either a clause boundary or a LocalAgreement-2 confirmed prefix.

faqItems.question: How do I prevent Speaker A's translated voice from being picked up by Speaker B's microphone and translated back?
faqItems.answer: In WebRTC calls, route separate directional audio tracks per participant. On shared speakerphones in a physical room, implement a half-duplex acoustic ducking gate that suppresses STT input while TTS playback is active.

faqItems.question: Can I use Meta's SeamlessM4T or NLLB-200 models in a commercial SaaS product?
faqItems.answer: No—both SeamlessM4T and NLLB-200 are released under the CC-BY-NC-4.0 (Non-Commercial) licence. For commercial self-hosting, use Apache-2.0 licensed LLMs like Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct via Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama).

faqItems.question: How do I ensure company product names and medical/legal terms are translated accurately?
faqItems.answer: Inject a deterministic domain glossary (glossary={"Signal Desk": "Signal Desk"}) into both the STT keyterm list and the translation system prompt.

faqItems.question: Why is `chrF` preferred over standard word-level `BLEU` for evaluating translation quality?
faqItems.answer: Word-level BLEU penalises morphologically rich languages (like Hindi, German, Turkish, or Russian) harshly when a word stem is correct but an inflection suffix differs slightly, whereas character $n$-gram F-score (chrF) rewards partial morphological overlap and correlates better with human ratings.

faqItems.question: What is the ideal end-to-end ear-to-voice latency for live interpretation?
faqItems.answer: Professional human simultaneous interpreters operate at a 2.0 to 3.0-second lag ("ear-voice span") so they can hear the verb of the clause. Aim for 1.2 to 2.2 seconds of clause-buffered latency.

faqItems.question: How do I preserve the speaker's emotional tone or formality level?
faqItems.answer: Set a conversation register parameter (formal vs casual) in RollingTranslationContext so the translator consistently selects polite pronouns (usted / आप / Sie).

faqItems.question: How do I handle overlapping speech when both participants talk at the same time?
faqItems.answer: Because each participant streams on an independent WebRTC audio track (Track A and Track B), both STT+Translation pipelines run concurrently in full duplex without corrupting each other's audio.

body:
## Introduction

To build a real-time AI translation system for live voice conversations between two speakers speaking different languages, you must solve the Simultaneous Wait-$k$ / Clause-Boundary Dilemma: if you translate word-by-word as tokens arrive, differences in Subject-Verb-Object (SVO, like English) versus Subject-Object-Verb (SOV, like Hindi, Japanese, or German) word order produce garbled translations; if you wait for a speaker to finish a 30-second monologue, the conversation stalls. By combining LocalAgreement-2 streaming ASR (emitting confirmed transcript prefixes every 1.2–2.0 seconds), a rolling conversational context buffer with glossary constraints, and dual-channel speaker-isolated audio routing (to prevent acoustic feedback loops where Speaker A's translated TTS audio is re-transcribed by Speaker B's microphone stream), you can achieve sub-1.5-second simultaneous interpretation.

## Bidirectional Streaming Audio Translation Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    MicA([Speaker A Audio Stream: Language X]) --> VADA[Silero VAD + LocalAgreement ASR]
    VADA --> ClauseBuffer[Clause-Boundary Accumulator + Context Window]
    ClauseBuffer --> Translator[Low-Latency Translation Engine + Domain Glossary]
    Translator --> TTSB[Streaming TTS in Language Y]
    TTSB --> EarB([Speaker B Output Track + Ducking Gate])
    MicB([Speaker B Audio Stream: Language Y]) --> VADB[Silero VAD + LocalAgreement ASR]
    VADB --> ClauseBufferB[Clause-Boundary Accumulator]
    ClauseBufferB --> TranslatorB[Low-Latency Translation Engine]
    TranslatorB --> TTSA[Streaming TTS in Language X]
    TTSA --> EarA([Speaker A Output Track])
```

### Preventing Cross-Talk Echo & Preserving Conversational Context

1. Isolated Per-Participant Audio Tracks (WebRTC): In LiveKit (https://github.com/livekit/agents) or Pipecat (https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat), subscribe to Speaker A's isolated input track (ParticipantA.audio_track) and publish the translated TTS audio on a dedicated translation track subscribed only by Speaker B. If both speakers are in the same physical room using a single speakerphone, apply a Half-Duplex Acoustic Ducking Gate that mutes inbound STT capture while translated TTS playback is active (plus a 150ms tail buffer).
1. Rolling Context & Pronoun Resolution: Spoken sentences frequently drop pronouns (*"Will ship tomorrow"*). Passing the last 3 translated utterance pairs alongside a domain glossary dictionary ensures consistent terminology and gender/formality agreement (tú vs usted, तुम vs आप).

## Technology Comparison: Paid vs. Open-Source Translation Stack

| Component | Commercial API | Open-Source / Open-Weight Alternative | Self-Hosting Possible? | Latency & Quality Trade-offs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Streaming Speech Recognition | Deepgram Nova-3 Streaming (https://deepgram.com/pricing) (\$0.0092/min multilingual) | Faster-Whisper (https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) + LocalAgreement-2 (WhisperLiveKit / whisper_streaming) | Yes (GPU required for real-time) | LocalAgreement-2 confirms tokens when two consecutive sliding audio windows agree on the prefix. |
| Neural Translation Model | OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini) / DeepL API / Google Cloud Translate | Meta SeamlessM4T-v2 / NLLB-200-distilled-1.3B (CC-BY-NC-4.0 — *non-commercial*) / Qwen2.5-14B via Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (Apache-2.0 — *commercial allowed*) | Yes | Critical Licence Check: Meta's NLLB-200 and SeamlessM4T weights are licensed under CC-BY-NC-4.0 (Non-Commercial). For commercial self-hosting, use Apache-2.0 licensed Qwen2.5 or Gemma models. |
| Streaming TTS | Deepgram Aura-2 (https://deepgram.com/pricing) / Cartesia Sonic / ElevenLabs Flash | OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl (https://github.com/OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl) / Kokoro-82M | Yes | Streaming TTS must support chunked PCM output at <180ms TTFB. |

### Recommended Implementation Options

### Option A: Best Practical Commercial Implementation (Recommended): LiveKit Agents (https://github.com/livekit/agents) WebRTC rooms + Deepgram Nova-3 Streaming STT + gpt-4o-mini (with rolling context & glossary) + Cartesia/Deepgram streaming TTS.

### Option B: Commercial-Permissive Open-Source Stack: Pipecat (https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat) + Faster-Whisper (https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) LocalAgreement streaming + local Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) running Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct (Apache-2.0) + local TTS.

### Option C: Research & Non-Commercial Speech-to-Speech Stack: Meta SeamlessM4T-v2 or WhisperLiveKit (QUENTINFUXA/WHISPERLIVEKIT (https://github.com/QUENTINFUXA/WHISPERLIVEKIT)).

## Step-by-Step Implementation Guide

### Step 1: Project Structure

```text
realtime-voice-translator/
├── app/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── local_agreement.py
│   └── context_translator.py
├── tests/
│   └── test_voice_translator.py
└── requirements.txt
```

### Step 2: Implement the LocalAgreement-2 Streaming Prefix Buffer (app/local_agreement.py)

When running streaming ASR over sliding audio chunks, the last few words at the right edge of an audio chunk often change as the next 0.5 seconds of audio arrives. The LocalAgreement-2 algorithm emits only the longest common word prefix agreed upon by two consecutive ASR hypotheses, preventing flickering mistranslations:

```python
from typing import List

class LocalAgreementBuffer:
    """Emits confirmed streaming ASR tokens using the LocalAgreement-2 prefix policy."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.prev_hypothesis: List[str] = []
        self.committed_words: List[str] = []

    def update_and_get_newly_confirmed(self, current_hypothesis_text: str) -> str:
        curr_words = current_hypothesis_text.strip().split()
        if not self.prev_hypothesis:
            self.prev_hypothesis = curr_words
            return ""

        # Find longest common prefix between prev_hypothesis and curr_words
        common_prefix_len = 0
        for w_prev, w_curr in zip(self.prev_hypothesis, curr_words):
            if w_prev.lower() == w_curr.lower():
                common_prefix_len += 1
            else:
                break

        already_committed_len = len(self.committed_words)
        if common_prefix_len > already_committed_len:
            new_words = curr_words[already_committed_len:common_prefix_len]
            self.committed_words.extend(new_words)
            self.prev_hypothesis = curr_words
            return " ".join(new_words)

        self.prev_hypothesis = curr_words
        return ""
```

### Step 3: Implement Rolling Context Translation & BLEU/chrF Quality Scoring (app/context_translator.py)

```python
from collections import deque
from typing import Dict, Deque, Tuple, Counter
import math

class RollingTranslationContext:
    def __init__(self, source_lang: str, target_lang: str, glossary: Dict[str, str] | None = None, max_turns: int = 4):
        self.source_lang = source_lang
        self.target_lang = target_lang
        self.glossary = glossary or {}
        self.history: Deque[Tuple[str, str]] = deque(maxlen=max_turns)

    def build_translation_prompt(self, new_utterance: str) -> str:
        glossary_lines = "\n".join(f"- '{k}' MUST be translated as '{v}'" for k, v in self.glossary.items())
        history_lines = "\n".join(f"Source: {s}\nTarget: {t}" for s, t in self.history)
        return (
            f"Translate spoken {self.source_lang} into natural spoken {self.target_lang}.\n"
            f"Glossary Rules:\n{glossary_lines or 'None'}\n\n"
            f"Recent Conversation Context:\n{history_lines or 'None'}\n\n"
            f"Current Utterance to Translate:\n{new_utterance}"
        )

    def record_turn(self, source_text: str, translated_text: str) -> None:
        self.history.append((source_text, translated_text))

def compute_chrf_score(reference: str, hypothesis: str, n_max: int = 6, beta: float = 2.0) -> float:
    """Computes character n-gram F-score (chrF) for evaluating translation quality across morphologies."""
    ref_clean = reference.strip()
    hyp_clean = hypothesis.strip()
    if not ref_clean or not hyp_clean:
        return 0.0

    total_prec = 0.0
    total_rec = 0.0
    valid_orders = 0

    for n in range(1, n_max + 1):
        if len(ref_clean) < n or len(hyp_clean) < n:
            continue
        ref_ngrams = Counter(ref_clean[i : i + n] for i in range(len(ref_clean) - n + 1))
        hyp_ngrams = Counter(hyp_clean[i : i + n] for i in range(len(hyp_clean) - n + 1))
        overlap = sum((ref_ngrams & hyp_ngrams).values())
        total_prec += overlap / sum(hyp_ngrams.values())
        total_rec += overlap / sum(ref_ngrams.values())
        valid_orders += 1

    if valid_orders == 0 or (total_prec + total_rec) == 0:
        return 0.0
    avg_p = total_prec / valid_orders
    avg_r = total_rec / valid_orders
    beta_sq = beta ** 2
    chrf = ((1 + beta_sq) * avg_p * avg_r) / ((beta_sq * avg_p) + avg_r)
    return round(chrf * 100.0, 2)
```

## Testing the Real-Time Translation Pipeline (tests/test_voice_translator.py)

```python
from app.local_agreement import LocalAgreementBuffer
from app.context_translator import RollingTranslationContext, compute_chrf_score

def test_local_agreement_commits_only_stable_prefixes():
    buf = LocalAgreementBuffer()
    # Window 1 partial hypothesis
    assert buf.update_and_get_newly_confirmed("We need to review the contract") == ""
    # Window 2 agrees on "We need to review" but changes "the contract" -> "the SLA terms"
    confirmed_1 = buf.update_and_get_newly_confirmed("We need to review the SLA terms")
    assert confirmed_1 == "We need to review the"
    # Window 3 agrees on "SLA terms tomorrow"
    confirmed_2 = buf.update_and_get_newly_confirmed("We need to review the SLA terms tomorrow")
    assert confirmed_2 == "SLA terms"

def test_rolling_context_and_chrf_metric():
    ctx = RollingTranslationContext("English", "Spanish", glossary={"Transactional Outbox": "Bandeja de salida transaccional"})
    ctx.record_turn("Good morning.", "Buenos días.")
    prompt = ctx.build_translation_prompt("We deployed the Transactional Outbox.")
    assert "Bandeja de salida transaccional" in prompt
    assert "Buenos días." in prompt

    score = compute_chrf_score("Buenos días, ¿cómo estás?", "Buenos días, ¿cómo está usted?")
    assert score > 55.0
```

## Cost Considerations & Production Checklist

- Licence Verification Reminder: Never deploy Meta's NLLB-200 or SeamlessM4T weights in a commercial paid product without a commercial licence, as their model cards specify CC-BY-NC-4.0 (Non-Commercial). Use Qwen2.5 (Apache-2.0), Gemma (Gemma Terms of Use), or commercial APIs (gpt-4o-mini / DeepL) for commercial products.
- Cost Breakdown: Bidirectional streaming STT + translation + TTS costs \~\$0.035/minute on commercial APIs or \$0 API cost on a single 24GB GPU server running Faster-Whisper + Qwen2.5 + Kokoro/Piper.

## Useful Tools, Documentation and GitHub Repositories

| Resource | Purpose | Type | Link |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LiveKit Agents | Multi-participant WebRTC audio track routing | Open-Source (Apache-2.0) | https://github.com/livekit/agents |
| Pipecat | Streaming audio and translation pipeline orchestration | Open-Source (BSD-2) | https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat |
| WhisperLiveKit | Real-time local speech-to-text with LocalAgreement | Open-Source | https://github.com/QUENTINFUXA/WHISPERLIVEKIT |
| Faster-Whisper | CTranslate2 Whisper inference engine | Open-Source (MIT) | https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper |

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why shouldn't I translate every word immediately as the STT model emits interim results?

Interim STT hypotheses change frequently as acoustic context arrives, and SOV/SVO languages invert verb positions. Translating unconfirmed interim tokens causes the TTS voice to repeat and contradict itself mid-sentence. Wait for either a clause boundary or a LocalAgreement-2 confirmed prefix.

### How do I prevent Speaker A's translated voice from being picked up by Speaker B's microphone and translated back?

In WebRTC calls, route separate directional audio tracks per participant. On shared speakerphones in a physical room, implement a half-duplex acoustic ducking gate that suppresses STT input while TTS playback is active.

### Can I use Meta's SeamlessM4T or NLLB-200 models in a commercial SaaS product?

No—both SeamlessM4T and NLLB-200 are released under the CC-BY-NC-4.0 (Non-Commercial) licence. For commercial self-hosting, use Apache-2.0 licensed LLMs like Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct via Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama).

### How do I ensure company product names and medical/legal terms are translated accurately?

Inject a deterministic domain glossary (glossary={"Signal Desk": "Signal Desk"}) into both the STT keyterm list and the translation system prompt.

### Why is `chrF` preferred over standard word-level `BLEU` for evaluating translation quality?

Word-level BLEU penalises morphologically rich languages (like Hindi, German, Turkish, or Russian) harshly when a word stem is correct but an inflection suffix differs slightly, whereas character $n$-gram F-score (chrF) rewards partial morphological overlap and correlates better with human ratings.

### What is the ideal end-to-end ear-to-voice latency for live interpretation?

Professional human simultaneous interpreters operate at a 2.0 to 3.0-second lag ("ear-voice span") so they can hear the verb of the clause. Aim for 1.2 to 2.2 seconds of clause-buffered latency.

### How do I preserve the speaker's emotional tone or formality level?

Set a conversation register parameter (formal vs casual) in RollingTranslationContext so the translator consistently selects polite pronouns (usted / आप / Sie).

### How do I handle overlapping speech when both participants talk at the same time?

Because each participant streams on an independent WebRTC audio track (Track A and Track B), both STT+Translation pipelines run concurrently in full duplex without corrupting each other's audio.

body:
## Introduction

To build an AI video assistant that watches 60-minute lectures, product demos, security recordings, or engineering screen-shares and answers questions with exact [MM:SS] playable timestamps, you cannot sample every video frame at 30 frames per second (FPS). A 1-hour 1080p video at 30 FPS contains 108,000 frames—passing all of them to a Vision-Language Model (VLM) would consume over 80 million image tokens (\~\$200+ per video). Instead, an efficient multimodal video pipeline combines content-aware scene boundary detection ([PySceneDetect](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/Breakthrough/PySceneDetect) / perceptual frame hashing) to extract only distinct visual keyframes (reducing 108,000 frames to \~120–250 keyframes), word-timestamped audio transcription ([Faster-Whisper](https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper)), and temporally aligned multimodal chunks indexed in [Qdrant](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant) or [pgvector](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector).

## Multimodal Video Ingestion & Timestamp Retrieval Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Video([Input Video .mp4 / .mkv]) --> Demux[FFmpeg Audio/Video Demultiplexer]
    Demux --> AudioTrack[16kHz Audio Track]
    Demux --> VideoTrack[Video Frame Stream]
    AudioTrack --> Whisper[Faster-Whisper Word-Timestamp STT]
    VideoTrack --> SceneDetect[PySceneDetect + Perceptual Diff Keyframe Extractor]
    SceneDetect --> VLM[Vision-Language Model: Frame OCR & Visual Captioning]
    Whisper --> Aligner[Temporal Window Merger: 30s Segments + Keyframe Captions]
    VLM --> Aligner
    Aligner --> VectorIndex[(Qdrant / pgvector Multimodal Timestamp Index)]
    UserQ([User Question]) --> HybridQuery[Retrieve Top-K Timestamp Windows + Inspect High-Res Frames]
    VectorIndex --> HybridQuery
    HybridQuery --> Answer([Answer with Exact [MM:SS - MM:SS] Deep Links])
```

### Why Content-Aware Scene Detection Beats Uniform 1-FPS Sampling

In a recorded webinar, coding tutorial, or slide presentation, a speaker may stay on the same architecture slide for 4 minutes (generating 240 identical frames at 1 FPS) and then rapidly flip through 3 terminal windows in 5 seconds. Content-aware scene detection (computing mean pixel HSV/luminance delta $\Delta_{\text{frame}} \ge \theta$ combined with a maximum interval cap of 15 seconds) captures every slide transition and code change while eliminating 98% of redundant duplicate frames.

## Technology Comparison: Paid vs. Open-Source Video Stack

| Component | Commercial / Cloud API | Open-Source / Self-Hosted Alternative | Self-Hosting Possible? | Technical & Storage Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Scene & Keyframe Extraction | AWS Rekognition Video / Google Video Intelligence | PySceneDetect (https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/Breakthrough/PySceneDetect) (BSD-3-Clause) + OpenCV (opencv-python, Apache-2.0) + FFmpeg | Yes (runs fast on CPU) | Resize extracted keyframes to max 1024px long edge before VLM inference to reduce image token cost by 60%. |
| Audio Transcription | Deepgram Nova-3 (https://deepgram.com/pricing) | Faster-Whisper (https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) (MIT) | Yes | Aligns spoken explanations with visual slide changes. |
| Vision-Language Model (VLM) | Gemini 2.5 Pro / OpenAI gpt-4o-mini | Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (Qwen2.5-VL-7B / Qwen2.5-VL-32B / Gemma 4) | Yes | Qwen2.5-VL excels at reading dense terminal text and slide diagrams inside video frames. |
| Timestamp Vector Index | Pinecone / TwelveLabs | Qdrant (https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant) (Apache-2.0) / pgvector (https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector) | Yes | Store video_id, start_sec, end_sec, and keyframe_path in the vector payload. |

### Recommended Implementation Options

### Option A: Best Practical Implementation (Recommended): Python 3.12 + OpenCV/PySceneDetect (https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/Breakthrough/PySceneDetect) + Faster-Whisper (https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) + VLM frame captioning (gpt-4o-mini or Qwen2.5-VL) + Qdrant (https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant) timestamp retrieval.

### Option B: Fully Open-Source Local Implementation: OpenCV + PySceneDetect (https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/Breakthrough/PySceneDetect) + Faster-Whisper (https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) + local Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (qwen2.5-vl) + Qdrant (https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant).

### Option C: Production Video Knowledge Platform: FastAPI + S3/CloudFront HLS streaming + Celery GPU ingestion workers + Qdrant hybrid dense/sparse search.

## Step-by-Step Implementation Guide

### Step 1: Project Structure

```text
ai-video-assistant/
├── app/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── keyframe_selector.py
│   └── multimodal_aligner.py
├── tests/
│   └── test_video_assistant.py
└── requirements.txt
```

### Step 2: Implement Perceptual Scene Change Keyframe Selection (app/keyframe_selector.py)

```python
from typing import List
import numpy as np
from pydantic import BaseModel

class ExtractedKeyframe(BaseModel):
    frame_index: int
    timestamp_sec: float
    mean_diff_score: float

def select_scene_keyframes_from_luma(
    frame_luma_arrays: List[np.ndarray],
    fps: float,
    diff_threshold: float = 18.0,
    min_interval_sec: float = 1.5,
    max_interval_sec: float = 15.0,
) -> List[ExtractedKeyframe]:
    """Selects keyframes when visual scene change exceeds diff_threshold or max_interval_sec elapses."""
    if not frame_luma_arrays or fps <= 0:
        return []

    selected: List[ExtractedKeyframe] = [
        ExtractedKeyframe(frame_index=0, timestamp_sec=0.0, mean_diff_score=100.0)
    ]
    last_selected_frame = frame_luma_arrays[0].astype(np.float32)
    last_ts = 0.0

    for idx in range(1, len(frame_luma_arrays)):
        curr_ts = round(idx / fps, 2)
        elapsed = curr_ts - last_ts
        if elapsed < min_interval_sec:
            continue

        curr_arr = frame_luma_arrays[idx].astype(np.float32)
        mean_diff = float(np.mean(np.abs(curr_arr - last_selected_frame)))

        if mean_diff >= diff_threshold or elapsed >= max_interval_sec:
            selected.append(
                ExtractedKeyframe(
                    frame_index=idx,
                    timestamp_sec=curr_ts,
                    mean_diff_score=round(mean_diff, 2),
                )
            )
            last_selected_frame = curr_arr
            last_ts = curr_ts

    return selected
```

### Step 3: Align Audio Transcripts and Visual Captions into Timestamped RAG Chunks (app/multimodal_aligner.py)

```python
from typing import List
from pydantic import BaseModel

class TranscriptSegment(BaseModel):
    start_sec: float
    end_sec: float
    text: str

class VisualFrameCaption(BaseModel):
    timestamp_sec: float
    visual_description: str
    on_screen_ocr_text: str = ""

class MultimodalVideoChunk(BaseModel):
    video_id: str
    start_sec: float
    end_sec: float
    formatted_time_range: str
    combined_search_text: str

def format_mm_ss(seconds: float) -> str:
    mins = int(seconds // 60)
    secs = int(seconds % 60)
    return f"{mins:02d}:{secs:02d}"

def build_multimodal_video_chunks(
    video_id: str,
    transcripts: List[TranscriptSegment],
    visual_captions: List[VisualFrameCaption],
    window_sec: float = 30.0,
) -> List[MultimodalVideoChunk]:
    """Merges spoken transcript segments and visual frame descriptions into unified 30s retrieval windows."""
    max_time = max(
        max((t.end_sec for t in transcripts), default=0.0),
        max((v.timestamp_sec for v in visual_captions), default=0.0),
    )
    if max_time <= 0:
        return []

    chunks: List[MultimodalVideoChunk] = []
    curr_start = 0.0

    while curr_start < max_time:
        curr_end = curr_start + window_sec
        window_speech = [
            t.text.strip()
            for t in transcripts
            if t.end_sec > curr_start and t.start_sec < curr_end
        ]
        window_visuals = [
            f"[{format_mm_ss(v.timestamp_sec)} Screen: {v.visual_description} | OCR: {v.on_screen_ocr_text}]"
            for v in visual_captions
            if curr_start <= v.timestamp_sec < curr_end
        ]

        if window_speech or window_visuals:
            time_label = f"[{format_mm_ss(curr_start)} - {format_mm_ss(curr_end)}]"
            combined = (
                f"Video Timestamp {time_label}\n"
                f"Spoken Audio: {' '.join(window_speech) or 'No speech'}\n"
                f"Visual Scene: {' ; '.join(window_visuals) or 'Static scene'}"
            )
            chunks.append(
                MultimodalVideoChunk(
                    video_id=video_id,
                    start_sec=curr_start,
                    end_sec=curr_end,
                    formatted_time_range=time_label,
                    combined_search_text=combined,
                )
            )
        curr_start = curr_end

    return chunks
```

## Testing the Video Assistant (tests/test_video_assistant.py)

```python
import numpy as np
from app.keyframe_selector import select_scene_keyframes_from_luma
from app.multimodal_aligner import (
    TranscriptSegment,
    VisualFrameCaption,
    build_multimodal_video_chunks,
)

def test_scene_keyframe_deduplication_and_transition_detection():
    # 10 frames at 1 FPS: frames 0..4 are dark (luma=10), frames 5..9 switch to bright slide (luma=200)
    frames = [np.full((16, 16), 10, dtype=np.uint8) for _ in range(5)] + [
        np.full((16, 16), 200, dtype=np.uint8) for _ in range(5)
    ]
    keyframes = select_scene_keyframes_from_luma(frames, fps=1.0, diff_threshold=25.0, min_interval_sec=1.0)
    assert len(keyframes) == 2
    assert keyframes[0].frame_index == 0
    assert keyframes[1].frame_index == 5

def test_multimodal_window_alignment():
    speech = [TranscriptSegment(start_sec=2.0, end_sec=12.0, text="Here we configure the PostgreSQL HNSW index.")]
    visuals = [
        VisualFrameCaption(
            timestamp_sec=5.0,
            visual_description="Terminal window showing psql prompt",
            on_screen_ocr_text="CREATE INDEX ON items USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);",
        )
    ]
    chunks = build_multimodal_video_chunks("vid_01", speech, visuals, window_sec=30.0)
    assert len(chunks) == 1
    assert chunks[0].formatted_time_range == "[00:00 - 00:30]"
    assert "CREATE INDEX ON items USING hnsw" in chunks[0].combined_search_text
```

## Storage, Indexing & Cost Considerations

- Cost Breakdown: Extracting \~150 scene-change keyframes from a 60-minute video (at 250 tokens per resized keyframe = \~37,500 vision tokens) plus Faster-Whisper (https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) audio transcription costs \~\$0.02–$0.05 per hour of video on commercial mini VLMs or \$0 using local Qwen2.5-VL via Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama).

## Useful Tools, Documentation and GitHub Repositories

| Resource | Purpose | Type | Link |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PySceneDetect | Python/OpenCV video scene cut and boundary detection | Open-Source (BSD-3) | https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/Breakthrough/PySceneDetect |
| Faster-Whisper | Audio track transcription with word timestamps | Open-Source (MIT) | https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper |
| Qdrant | Vector search engine for multimodal timestamp payloads | Open-Source (Apache-2.0) | https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant |

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why shouldn't I just transcribe the audio track and ignore the video frames?

In coding tutorials, architecture walkthroughs, product demos, and silent security footage, critical information (commands typed in a terminal, chart numbers on a slide, or error stack traces) is never read aloud word-for-word by the speaker. Combining visual frame OCR/captions with audio transcripts makes on-screen text searchable.

### How much does scene-change detection reduce Vision LLM token costs compared to 1-FPS sampling?

A 60-minute presentation sampled at 1 FPS produces 3,600 frames. Scene-change detection (select_scene_keyframes_from_luma) typically yields 100–180 keyframes, cutting Vision LLM costs and ingestion time by 95%.

### How do I handle questions that require reading tiny text inside a specific code slide?

Follow a two-stage resolution strategy: index low-cost thumbnail captions (768p) for all keyframes during ingestion; when a user asks a question and top-3 timestamp windows are retrieved from Qdrant, load the original full-resolution 1080p/4K keyframe PNGs for just those 3 timestamps into the final VLM answer prompt.

### How do I link the AI's answer directly to the exact moment in the video player?

Instruct the LLM to cite the formatted_time_range ([04:30 - 05:00]) and parse [MM:SS] in your frontend into videoElement.currentTime = minutes * 60 + seconds.

### What if a speaker talks across the boundary of two 30-second windows (e.g., at `00:29`)?

Use a 5-second sliding overlap (step = 25s, window = 30s) or align chunk boundaries directly to natural PySceneDetect scene cuts and Whisper sentence pauses.

### Can I index silent CCTV or manufacturing inspection videos with this architecture?

Yes; when transcripts is empty, build_multimodal_video_chunks indexes purely on window_visuals accompanied by max_interval_sec=5.0 keyframe sampling.

### Should I store raw base64 images inside Qdrant or PostgreSQL vector rows?

No—storing multi-megabyte base64 strings inside vector payloads bloats RAM and slows HNSW traversal. Store keyframe JPEGs in object storage (S3/MinIO) and store only the s3_key and extracted text caption in Qdrant.

### Can this entire video assistant run locally on a single GPU?

Yes; PySceneDetect (https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/Breakthrough/PySceneDetect) runs on CPU, while Faster-Whisper (https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) and Qwen2.5-VL-7B via Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) fit together on a single 16GB–24GB GPU.

faqItems.question: Why use Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scales (BARS) instead of asking the LLM for a 1–100 score?
faqItems.answer: A 1–100 scale has arbitrary granularity—an LLM cannot meaningfully distinguish a "73" from a "76". A 1–5 BARS rubric defines explicit observable engineering behaviors for Level 1 (cannot explain basic indexing), Level 3 (designs standard B-tree indexes and explains read/write trade-offs), and Level 5 (diagnoses lock contention, partitioning, and HNSW recall tuning in production).

faqItems.question: How do I prevent the voice AI from cutting off a candidate who is pausing to think through a system design question?
faqItems.answer: Configure a longer VAD endpointing silence threshold (min_endpointing_delay=1.5 seconds) during interview sessions compared to customer support calls (0.5s), and allow candidates to hold a "Push to Think / Mute" key.

faqItems.question: What if the speech-to-text model mishears a technical term like `idempotency` as `item potency`?
faqItems.answer: Pass a domain keyterm list to the STT engine and instruct the BARS evaluator prompt to account for phonetic ASR homophones of technical terms, while displaying the live transcript so the candidate can clarify.

faqItems.question: How many follow-up probes should the AI ask per question?
faqItems.answer: Cap follow-up probes at 2 per competency (`max_probes=2`) so a single question never consumes the entire 30-minute interview slot.

faqItems.question: How should technical coding assessments be graded inside an AI interview?
faqItems.answer: Run the candidate's submitted code against deterministic unit tests (checking correctness, edge cases, and execution time) and use the LLM only to evaluate code readability, complexity explanation, and debugging process.

faqItems.question: What is a good Quadratic Weighted Kappa ($\kappa_w$) threshold before deploying an AI interviewer?
faqItems.answer: Industrial-organizational psychology standards recommend $\kappa_w \ge 0.75$ between the automated rubric scorer and calibrated human domain experts.

faqItems.question: Should an AI interviewer analyse facial expressions or eye tracking via webcam?
faqItems.answer: No. Affective webcam analysis (scoring "confidence" from facial micro-expressions or eye movement) lacks scientific validity, discriminates against neurodivergent candidates, and is restricted or banned under the EU AI Act and Illinois AIVIA.

faqItems.question: How do I detect if a candidate is reading verbatim from another AI screen during a remote interview?
faqItems.answer: Ask adaptive follow-up probes grounded in the candidate's specific design choices (*"In line 14 of your code, why did you choose a min-heap over quickselect if* $K$ *is fixed at 3?"*); real-time architectural trade-off probing naturally distinguishes genuine understanding from scripted reading.

body:
## Introduction

To build an AI interviewer that conducts structured technical or behavioural interviews and produces reliable, legally defensible candidate evaluations, you must replace open-ended LLM impressions with Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scales (BARS), bounded adaptive depth-probing, and deterministic code test-case execution. When an unstructured LLM conducts an interview, it often asks leading questions, penalises non-native speech disfluencies (*"um"*, pauses, regional accents), or exhibits recency bias. By structuring the interview as a finite state machine—where each competency has a standardized root question, up to 2 adaptive follow-up probes triggered only when specific rubric evidence is missing, and a 1-to-5 BARS rubric anchored to explicit behavioural indicators—you achieve high inter-rater reliability and fairness.

> [!TIP]
> **Architecture Reference:** Internal Link Suggestion: Connect this structured interview pipeline with [Article 5: How to Build an AI Recruitment Agent That Screens Resumes and Shortlists Candidates and [Article 17: How to Build an AI Phone Receptionist ](/writing/build-ai-recruitment-agent-resume-screening/](/writing/build-ai-phone-receptionist-twilio-voice-calls/)).

## Structured Interview Workflow & BARS Evaluation Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Consent([Candidate Informed Consent & Audio Check]) --> CompetencyLoop[Load Next Competency & Root Question]
    CompetencyLoop --> VoiceInteraction[LiveKit / Pipecat Voice Turn + Transcript Display]
    VoiceInteraction --> ProbeCheck{Evidence Completeness Analyzer: Situation, Action, Outcome?}
    ProbeCheck -- "Missing Detail & probes_used < 2" --> GenerateProbe[Ask Targeted Clarifying Probe]
    GenerateProbe --> VoiceInteraction
    ProbeCheck -- "Complete or probes_used == 2" --> CodeCheck{Includes Coding Task?}
    CodeCheck -- "Yes" --> CodeSandbox[Run Candidate Code Against Unit Test Suite]
    CodeCheck -- "No" --> BARSScorer[BARS 1-5 Rubric Evaluator with Verbatim Quotes]
    CodeSandbox --> BARSScorer
    BARSScorer --> Report([Human Hiring Manager Review Report + Audio/Code Artifacts])
```

### Bias Mitigation, Candidate Consent & Evaluation Reliability

1. Mandatory Informed Consent & Accommodations: Before recording a single audio frame, display a clear disclosure explaining how the AI interviewer operates, what competencies are evaluated, that a human hiring manager reviews all transcripts and scores, and provide a one-click option to request a traditional human interview or accessibility accommodation (e.g., extended response time or text-only mode).
1. Acoustic & Accent Fairness: Evaluate strictly on the semantic content of the transcript and executed code test cases—never on speech rate, pitch, filler word frequency, or accent. Show the live transcript on screen so the candidate can see and correct any ASR misrecognition of technical terms (*"idempotency"*, *"PostgreSQL"*).
1. Measuring Evaluation Reliability (Cohen's Quadratic Weighted Kappa $\kappa_w$): Validate your BARS evaluator against a benchmark set of 50 human-graded interview transcripts and require Quadratic Weighted Kappa $\kappa_w \ge 0.75$ before production deployment.

```python
from typing import Dict, List, Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class CompetencyBARSRubric(BaseModel):
    competency_id: str
    competency_name: str
    root_question: str
    max_probes: int = 2
    anchor_level_1_unsatisfactory: str
    anchor_level_3_proficient: str
    anchor_level_5_exceptional: str

class ProbeDecision(BaseModel):
    has_specific_example: bool
    has_technical_tradeoffs: bool
    has_measurable_outcome: bool
    should_ask_probe: bool
    next_probe_question: Optional[str] = None

def decide_deterministic_probe_gate(
    probes_already_asked: int,
    max_probes: int,
    has_specific_example: bool,
    has_technical_tradeoffs: bool,
    has_measurable_outcome: bool,
) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    """Deterministically decides whether to ask a follow-up probe or advance to the next competency."""
    if probes_already_asked >= max_probes:
        return False, "MAX_PROBES_REACHED"
    if not has_specific_example:
        return True, "MISSING_CONCRETE_EXAMPLE"
    if not has_technical_tradeoffs:
        return True, "MISSING_TECHNICAL_TRADEOFFS"
    if not has_measurable_outcome:
        return True, "MISSING_MEASURABLE_OUTCOME"
    return False, "EVIDENCE_COMPLETE"

class CompetencyScoreCard(BaseModel):
    competency_id: str
    bars_score: int = Field(..., ge=1, le=5)
    verbatim_candidate_quotes: List[str] = Field(..., min_length=1)
    matched_anchor_rationale: str
    coding_tests_passed: Optional[int] = None
    coding_tests_total: Optional[int] = None
```

### Step 3: Implement Quadratic Weighted Kappa ($\kappa_w$) for Evaluation Reliability (app/reliability_metrics.py)

To verify that your AI BARS evaluator agrees with human senior engineers across 1-to-5 ordinal scores, compute Quadratic Weighted Cohen's Kappa ($\kappa_w$):

```python
from typing import List

def compute_quadratic_weighted_kappa(
    human_scores: List[int],
    ai_scores: List[int],
    min_rating: int = 1,
    max_rating: int = 5,
) -> float:
    """Computes Quadratic Weighted Cohen's Kappa between human and AI ordinal 1-5 rubric ratings."""
    if len(human_scores) != len(ai_scores) or len(human_scores) == 0:
        raise ValueError("Score lists must be non-empty and of equal length.")

    num_classes = max_rating - min_rating + 1
    n = float(len(human_scores))

    # Observed confusion matrix O and marginal histograms
    obs = [[0.0] * num_classes for _ in range(num_classes)]
    hist_h = [0.0] * num_classes
    hist_a = [0.0] * num_classes

    for h, a in zip(human_scores, ai_scores):
        i = h - min_rating
        j = a - min_rating
        obs[i][j] += 1.0
        hist_h[i] += 1.0
        hist_a[j] += 1.0

    num = 0.0
    den = 0.0
    for i in range(num_classes):
        for j in range(num_classes):
            weight = float((i - j) ** 2) / float((num_classes - 1) ** 2)
            expected_ij = (hist_h[i] * hist_a[j]) / n
            num += weight * (obs[i][j] / n)
            den += weight * (expected_ij / n)

    if den == 0.0:
        return 1.0
    return round(1.0 - (num / den), 4)
```

```python
from app.bars_rubric import decide_deterministic_probe_gate
from app.reliability_metrics import compute_quadratic_weighted_kappa

def test_adaptive_probe_gate_stops_at_max_probes_or_complete_evidence():
    should_probe, reason = decide_deterministic_probe_gate(
        probes_already_asked=0,
        max_probes=2,
        has_specific_example=True,
        has_technical_tradeoffs=False,
        has_measurable_outcome=True,

    assert should_probe is True
    assert reason == "MISSING_TECHNICAL_TRADEOFFS"

    capped, cap_reason = decide_deterministic_probe_gate(
        probes_already_asked=2,
        max_probes=2,
        has_specific_example=False,
        has_technical_tradeoffs=False,
        has_measurable_outcome=False,
    )
    assert capped is False
    assert cap_reason == "MAX_PROBES_REACHED"

def test_quadratic_weighted_kappa_reliability():
    human = [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 4, 5, 3]
    ai_good = [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 4, 4, 3]
    kappa = compute_quadratic_weighted_kappa(human, ai_good)
    assert kappa > 0.90
```

- Never Auto-Reject Without Human Oversight: Present the CompetencyScoreCard alongside the playable audio timestamps, verbatim candidate quotes, and unit-test execution logs to the human hiring panel.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why use Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scales (BARS) instead of asking the LLM for a 1–100 score?

A 1–100 scale has arbitrary granularity—an LLM cannot meaningfully distinguish a "73" from a "76". A 1–5 BARS rubric defines explicit observable engineering behaviors for Level 1 (cannot explain basic indexing), Level 3 (designs standard B-tree indexes and explains read/write trade-offs), and Level 5 (diagnoses lock contention, partitioning, and HNSW recall tuning in production).

### How do I prevent the voice AI from cutting off a candidate who is pausing to think through a system design question?

Configure a longer VAD endpointing silence threshold (min_endpointing_delay=1.5 seconds) during interview sessions compared to customer support calls (0.5s), and allow candidates to hold a "Push to Think / Mute" key.

### What if the speech-to-text model mishears a technical term like `idempotency` as `item potency`?

Pass a domain keyterm list to the STT engine and instruct the BARS evaluator prompt to account for phonetic ASR homophones of technical terms, while displaying the live transcript so the candidate can clarify.

### How many follow-up probes should the AI ask per question?

Cap follow-up probes at 2 per competency (`max_probes=2`) so a single question never consumes the entire 30-minute interview slot.

### How should technical coding assessments be graded inside an AI interview?

Run the candidate's submitted code against deterministic unit tests (checking correctness, edge cases, and execution time) and use the LLM only to evaluate code readability, complexity explanation, and debugging process.

### What is a good Quadratic Weighted Kappa ($\kappa_w$) threshold before deploying an AI interviewer?

Industrial-organizational psychology standards recommend $\kappa_w \ge 0.75$ between the automated rubric scorer and calibrated human domain experts.

### Should an AI interviewer analyse facial expressions or eye tracking via webcam?

No. Affective webcam analysis (scoring "confidence" from facial micro-expressions or eye movement) lacks scientific validity, discriminates against neurodivergent candidates, and is restricted or banned under the EU AI Act and Illinois AIVIA.

### How do I detect if a candidate is reading verbatim from another AI screen during a remote interview?

Ask adaptive follow-up probes grounded in the candidate's specific design choices (*"In line 14 of your code, why did you choose a min-heap over quickselect if* $K$ *is fixed at 3?"*); real-time architectural trade-off probing naturally distinguishes genuine understanding from scripted reading.

faqItems.answer: The ZPD consists of skills whose prerequisite nodes in the curriculum DAG are mastered ($P(L) \ge 0.95$) while the target skill itself has $0.25 \le P(L) < 0.85$. Selecting practice problems from the ZPD keeps students challenged without overwhelming them.

faqItems.question: How many consecutive wrong attempts should trigger a worked example?
faqItems.answer: After 3 consecutive errors (HintLevel.LEVEL_3_WORKED_ANALOGY), asking more open-ended Socratic questions causes frustration. Show a worked step-by-step solution to a *similar analogous problem* and then ask the student to apply that same step to their current problem.

body:
## Introduction

To build an AI tutor that genuinely helps students master mathematics, programming, or science through interactive conversations, you must solve the "Homework Vending Machine" Problem: out of the box, general-purpose LLMs immediately hand the student the final answer when asked a homework question, short-circuiting active learning. An effective AI tutor combines a Socratic Scaffolding State Machine (which withholds direct answers and walks the student through a 4-level hint ladder), Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) to track mastery probability $P(L_t)$ across curriculum skills, curriculum-grounded RAG, and deterministic mathematical/code verification.

## Personalised Socratic Tutoring & Knowledge Tracing Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Student([Student Response / Question]) --> Guardrail[Age-Appropriate & PII Safety Filter]
    Guardrail --> Verifier[Deterministic Math / Code Step Verifier]
    Verifier --> BKT[Bayesian Knowledge Tracing Engine: Update Mastery P_L]
    BKT --> PedagogicalState{Socratic Hint Ladder Controller: Level 1..4}
    PedagogicalState -- "Level 1: Metacognitive Question" --> CurriculumRAG[Retrieve Verified Textbook Concept Chunk]
    PedagogicalState -- "Level 2: Conceptual Hint" --> CurriculumRAG
    PedagogicalState -- "Level 3: Worked Analogous Step" --> CurriculumRAG
    PedagogicalState -- "Level 4: Guided Solution + Check" --> CurriculumRAG
    CurriculumRAG --> TutorLLM[Socratic Response Generator + Spoilers Gate]
    TutorLLM --> Output([Interactive Socratic Prompt + Updated Mastery Dashboard])
```

### How Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) Updates Skill Mastery

For every granular learning objective (e.g., quadratic_factoring or python_for_loops), Bayesian Knowledge Tracing maintains the probability $P(L_t)$ that the student has mastered the skill using four parameters:

- $P(L_0)$: Initial prior mastery probability (e.g., 0.20).
- $P(T)$: Probability of transitioning from unlearned to learned after a practice step (e.g., 0.15).
- $P(S)$: Slip probability — probability a student who knows the skill makes a careless mistake (e.g., 0.10).
- $P(G)$: Guess probability — probability a student who does not know the skill guesses right (e.g., 0.20).

After observing whether the student's current step is correct (obs = True) or incorrect (obs = False), we compute the posterior $P(L_t \mid \text{obs})$ via Bayes' Rule and update mastery:

$$

P(L_t) = P(L_t \mid \text{obs}) + \bigl(1 - P(L_t \mid \text{obs})\bigr) \cdot P(T)

$$

When $P(L_t) \ge 0.95$, the skill is marked as Mastered and the adaptive question generator unlocks the next prerequisite node in the curriculum DAG.

## Technology Comparison: Paid vs. Open-Source EdTech Stack

| Component | Commercial Solution | Open-Source Alternative | Self-Hosting Possible? | Pedagogical & Privacy Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Symbolic Math Verification | WolframAlpha API | SymPy (BSD-3-Clause, Python symbolic algebra library) | Yes | Deterministically checks whether a student's intermediate algebraic equation is equivalent to the target equation. |
| Curriculum Content Store | Commercial Textbook APIs | OpenStax (CC-BY 4.0 textbooks) + pgvector (https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector) | Yes | Ground explanations in the student's exact grade-level curriculum terminology. |
| Student Data Privacy | Managed Cloud DLP | Presidio (https://github.com/microsoft/presidio) (MIT) + Pseudonymous Student IDs | Yes | Essential for FERPA, COPPA, and GDPR-K compliance. |

### Recommended Implementation Options

### Option A: Best Practical Implementation (Recommended): Python 3.12 + FastAPI + Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (bkt.py) + SymPy step equivalence checker + LangGraph (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph) Socratic Hint Ladder + OpenAI/Claude (or local Gemma 4).

### Option B: 100% Open-Source School Server Stack: Local Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) + SymPy + pgvector (https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector) indexed with OpenStax CC-BY textbooks + PostgreSQL.

### Option C: Production Multimodal Voice/Whiteboard Tutor: LiveKit Agents (https://github.com/livekit/agents) + KaTeX math rendering + BKT learning analytics dashboard for teachers.

## Step-by-Step Implementation Guide

### Step 1: Project Structure

```text
ai-socratic-tutor/
├── app/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── bkt_engine.py
```

### Step 2: Implement the Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) Engine (app/bkt_engine.py)

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class SkillMasteryState(BaseModel):
    skill_id: str
    p_mastery: float = Field(0.20, ge=0.0, le=1.0, description="Current P(L_t)")
    p_transit: float = Field(0.15, ge=0.0, le=1.0, description="P(T) learning rate")
    p_slip: float = Field(0.10, ge=0.0, le=0.49, description="P(S) careless slip rate")
    p_guess: float = Field(0.20, ge=0.0, le=0.49, description="P(G) lucky guess rate")
    attempts: int = 0
    consecutive_errors: int = 0

    @property
    def is_mastered(self) -> bool:
        return self.p_mastery >= 0.95

def update_bkt_mastery(state: SkillMasteryState, is_correct: bool) -> SkillMasteryState:
    """Updates student skill mastery probability P(L_t) using exact Bayesian Knowledge Tracing."""
    p_l = state.p_mastery
    p_t = state.p_transit
    p_s = state.p_slip
    p_g = state.p_guess

    if is_correct:
        # P(L | correct) = [P(L)*(1 - P(S))] / [P(L)*(1 - P(S)) + (1 - P(L))*P(G)]
        num = p_l * (1.0 - p_s)
        den = num + ((1.0 - p_l) * p_g)
        posterior = num / den if den > 0 else p_l
        consecutive_err = 0
    else:
        # P(L | incorrect) = [P(L)*P(S)] / [P(L)*P(S) + (1 - P(L))*(1 - P(G))]
        num = p_l * p_s
        den = num + ((1.0 - p_l) * (1.0 - p_g))
        posterior = num / den if den > 0 else p_l
        consecutive_err = state.consecutive_errors + 1

    new_p_mastery = posterior + ((1.0 - posterior) * p_t)
    return state.model_copy(
        update={
            "p_mastery": round(min(0.999, max(0.001, new_p_mastery)), 4),
            "attempts": state.attempts + 1,
            "consecutive_errors": consecutive_err,
        }
    )
```

### Step 3: Implement the Socratic Hint Ladder & Anti-Spoiler Guardrail (app/socratic_ladder.py)

```python
from enum import IntEnum
from pydantic import BaseModel

class HintLevel(IntEnum):
    LEVEL_1_SOCRATIC_QUESTION = 1
    LEVEL_2_CONCEPTUAL_HINT = 2
    LEVEL_3_WORKED_ANALOGY = 3
    LEVEL_4_GUIDED_STEP_SOLUTION = 4

def select_socratic_hint_level(consecutive_errors: int) -> HintLevel:
    """Escalates scaffolding support gradually based on consecutive student struggles."""
    if consecutive_errors <= 1:
        return HintLevel.LEVEL_1_SOCRATIC_QUESTION
    if consecutive_errors == 2:
        return HintLevel.LEVEL_2_CONCEPTUAL_HINT
    if consecutive_errors == 3:
        return HintLevel.LEVEL_3_WORKED_ANALOGY
    return HintLevel.LEVEL_4_GUIDED_STEP_SOLUTION

def verify_no_answer_spoiler(tutor_response: str, canonical_final_answer: str, current_level: HintLevel) -> bool:
    """Ensures the tutor does not leak the final answer string before HintLevel 4."""
    if current_level < HintLevel.LEVEL_4_GUIDED_STEP_SOLUTION:
        if canonical_final_answer.strip().lower() in tutor_response.lower():
            return False
    return True
```

## Testing the AI Tutor (tests/test_ai_tutor.py)

```python
from app.bkt_engine import SkillMasteryState, update_bkt_mastery
from app.socratic_ladder import (
    HintLevel,
    select_socratic_hint_level,
    verify_no_answer_spoiler,
)

def test_bkt_mastery_progression_reaches_mastery_after_correct_streak():
    state = SkillMasteryState(skill_id="linear_equations_1")
    for _ in range(6):
        state = update_bkt_mastery(state, is_correct=True)
    assert state.p_mastery >= 0.95
    assert state.is_mastered is True

def test_bkt_incorrect_answer_lowers_posterior_and_escalates_hint_level():
    state = SkillMasteryState(skill_id="fractions_add", p_mastery=0.50)
    state = update_bkt_mastery(state, is_correct=False)
    assert state.p_mastery < 0.50
    assert state.consecutive_errors == 1
    assert select_socratic_hint_level(state.consecutive_errors) == HintLevel.LEVEL_1_SOCRATIC_QUESTION

    state = update_bkt_mastery(state, is_correct=False)
    assert select_socratic_hint_level(state.consecutive_errors) == HintLevel.LEVEL_2_CONCEPTUAL_HINT

def test_anti_spoiler_gate_blocks_premature_answer_leak():
    assert verify_no_answer_spoiler(
        "What happens if you subtract 5 from both sides?",
        canonical_final_answer="x = 12",
        current_level=HintLevel.LEVEL_1_SOCRATIC_QUESTION,
    ) is True

    assert verify_no_answer_spoiler(
        "The answer is x = 12.",
        canonical_final_answer="x = 12",
        current_level=HintLevel.LEVEL_1_SOCRATIC_QUESTION,
    ) is False
```

- Cost Breakdown: A 30-turn interactive tutoring session costs \~\$0.008–$0.02 per session on commercial mini models or \$0 on local Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (Gemma 4).

Enforce the Socratic Hint Ladder in code (select_socratic_hint_level) and run verify_no_answer_spoiler() on the generated response before sending it to the student. If verify_no_answer_spoiler() returns False at Levels 1–3, regenerate the response with a stricter hint constraint.

### Why shouldn't the LLM check whether the student's math step is correct?

LLMs can be persuaded by confident-sounding student errors (*"Isn't* $2^3 = 6$*?"*). Parse algebraic expressions with SymPy (sympy.simplify(student_expr - target_expr) == 0) so step correctness is verified deterministically before updating Bayesian Knowledge Tracing.

### What is the Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) and how does the tutor use it?

The ZPD consists of skills whose prerequisite nodes in the curriculum DAG are mastered ($P(L) \ge 0.95$) while the target skill itself has $0.25 \le P(L) < 0.85$. Selecting practice problems from the ZPD keeps students challenged without overwhelming them.

### How many consecutive wrong attempts should trigger a worked example?

After 3 consecutive errors (HintLevel.LEVEL_3_WORKED_ANALOGY), asking more open-ended Socratic questions causes frustration. Show a worked step-by-step solution to a *similar analogous problem* and then ask the student to apply that same step to their current problem.

### Can this tutor adapt to different grade levels (e.g., Grade 5 vs. First-Year University)?

Yes; store reading_grade_level and preferred_analogies on the student profile and retrieve explanations exclusively from the matching OpenStax grade-level textbook collection in pgvector (https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector).

### How do teachers monitor which students need human intervention?

Flag any student-skill pair where attempts >= 6 and p_mastery < 0.35 ("Wheel-Spinning Alert") on the teacher's analytics dashboard so the teacher can provide 1-on-1 help.

### Is Bayesian Knowledge Tracing better than Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT) for small cohorts?

Yes; BKT requires only 4 interpretable parameters per skill and works reliably from Day 1 without requiring 50,000 historical student interaction logs to train a recurrent neural network.

### Can I add voice interaction to this AI tutor for early readers?

Yes; wrap the Socratic tutor graph inside LiveKit Agents (https://github.com/livekit/agents) or Pipecat (https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat) so younger learners can speak their reasoning aloud.

faqItems.question: Why shouldn't an AI image description start with "Image of..." or "Picture showing..."?
faqItems.answer: Screen readers (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) already announce "Graphic" or "Image" when encountering an element. Starting alt text with "Image of..." causes the screen reader to say "Graphic, Image of...", wasting the user's time. Start directly with the subject and action.

faqItems.question: How should the AI describe charts and graphs for blind engineers or analysts?
faqItems.answer: Provide a 1-sentence summary of the trend in alt text, and automatically convert the chart's data points into an HTML <table> with <th scope="col"> headers inside <details> (render_accessible_figure_html) so the user can navigate rows and columns using standard screen-reader table shortcuts (Ctrl+Alt+Arrow in NVDA/JAWS).

faqItems.question: Why is logical reading order critical when reading two-column PDFs aloud?
faqItems.answer: If an OCR script reads across the full horizontal width of a two-column PDF page, it reads line 1 of Column A followed immediately by line 1 of Column B, rendering the audio completely incomprehensible. Layout-aware parsers like Docling (https://github.com/docling-project/docling) segment bounding boxes by column first.

faqItems.question: What is the difference between `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-live="assertive"`?
faqItems.answer: aria-live="polite" waits until the screen reader finishes speaking the current element before announcing the status update, whereas aria-live="assertive" interrupts the screen reader immediately. Use polite for progress updates and reserve assertive strictly for critical errors or safety warnings.

faqItems.question: How do I support users with dyslexia alongside blind users?
faqItems.answer: Pair synchronized sentence/word visual highlighting (<mark>) with high-contrast customizable themes (>= 4.5:1 verified by compute_wcag_contrast_ratio), generous line spacing (line-height: 1.6), and adjustable TTS playback speeds.

faqItems.question: Yes; maintain the image in the VLM conversation context so the user can ask voice or text follow-ups like *"What is the expiration date printed on the bottom right corner of the box?
How do I protect user privacy when the accessibility assistant reads personal mail or medical prescriptions?
faqItems.answer: Default to local on-device or self-hosted inference via Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama) (Qwen2.5-VL) and never log or retain uploaded camera images on disk after the session ends.

faqItems.question: What playback speeds should an accessible document reader support?
faqItems.answer: Support increments from 0.75x up to 3.0x with pitch preservation (using time-scale modification / WSOLA so speeding up the voice does not raise its pitch like a chipmunk).

## Introduction To build an AI accessibility assistant for blind, low-vision, dyslexic, and print-disabled users that describes complex images and reads multi-column PDF documents aloud, you must design around WCAG 2.2 Level AA standards, screen-reader compatibility (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver), and progressive disclosure. Many untagged PDFs fail screen-reader users because two-column layouts, tables without scope attributes, and complex charts are read out as a jumbled stream of disconnected words or skipped entirely as "graphic". By combining layout-aware document reconstruction ([Docling](https://github.com/docling-project/docling)), two-tier Vision-Language image description (concise 1-sentence alt-text paired with an on-demand structured spatial/data breakdown), WCAG contrast and heading hierarchy verification, and sentence-synchronized Neural TTS with variable playback speed (`0.75x` to `2.5x`), you empower users to navigate visual and document content independently. ## Multimodal Accessibility & Screen-Reader Integration Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD Input([Untagged PDF / Image / Camera Frame]) --> Router{Document or Standalone Image?} Router -- "Untagged / Scanned PDF" --> Docling[Docling + PaddleOCR Layout & Reading-Order Parser] Router -- "Image / Chart / Diagram" --> VLM[Vision-Language Model: Alt-Text + Detailed Spatial Breakdown] Docling --> FigureExtract[Extract Embedded Figures & Tables] FigureExtract --> VLM Docling --> SemanticHTML[Accessible Semantic HTML5 Builder: H1-H6, Landmark, Table Scope] VLM --> SemanticHTML SemanticHTML --> WCAGValidator[Deterministic WCAG 2.2 Contrast & Structure Validator] WCAGValidator --> OutputUI([Screen-Reader ARIA UI + Synchronized Neural TTS Audio]) ``` ### Core WCAG 2.2 & Inclusive Design Engineering Principles 1. Progressive Disclosure for Image Descriptions (Brief vs. Detailed): Screen-reader users scanning a document do not want a 300-word essay every time focus lands on an icon or photo. Generate two distinct fields per visual asset: - concise_alt_text ($\le 125$ characters): Objective, immediate summary read automatically via alt="...". - extended_description: Structured spatial and data breakdown (e.g., converting a bar chart into an accessible with " in rendered ``` ## Deployment, Inclusive Design & Cost Considerations - Screen-Reader Live Announcements: When the Vision LLM is processing an uploaded PDF or camera image, emit status updates inside

so blind users receive immediate non-visual feedback that the application is working. - Cost Breakdown: Running Docling (https://github.com/docling-project/docling), PaddleOCR (https://www.paddleocr.ai/main/en/index.html), local Qwen2.5-VL via Ollama (https://github.com/ollama/ollama), and local Piper/Kokoro TTS has \$0 API cost and keeps sensitive personal documents 100% private. else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4 def compute_relative_luminance(hex_color: str) -> float: """Computes W3C WCAG 2.2 relative luminance L for a 6-digit hex color (#RRGGBB).""" clean =
